articles.title: Agents aren’t humans (but they kinda are)
articles.summary:
Agents aren’t humans (but they kinda are)
AI Agents now act on the web for millions of people. To a Site, an Agent can take many forms. It may be indistinguishable from a human user carrying out a task, or it might look like one visitor carrying many Users. This removes the ability for the Site to recognize, serve, and hold accountable the user or users behind the Agent, and causes the Site to face the costs when something goes wrong. This post argues that in order for Sites to maximize the access they provide to Agents, the ecosystem must develop new mechanisms to preserve the relationship between Sites and Users. Traditionally, in Security and Fraud Prevention, that requires three things: Identity, Reputation, and Accountability, allowing Sites to answer: Is the person acting being truthful about who they are? Is that person trustworthy? And who answers for the action?
“Personal AI Agents” (“Agents” for short) are automations that take instructions from a human (“User”) and pursue a goal by controlling a cloud computer or browser. They are usually hosted and maintained by an “Operator” as part of a managed service or consumer offering. Examples include Muse from Meta and dots from OpenAI, and more are launching all the time. Agents can potentially take any action online that their User could, without the limits that hold humans back. They don't tire, they run around the clock, they act in parallel, and they put up with friction no person would. Much of the web, from how Sit…

articles.title: Muse has a voice mode now
articles.summary:
Meta now lets you have voice conversations with your Muse AI agent in real time, CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced today.
Muse has a voice mode now
Muse AI agent now has voices and ‘expressive’ avatars that animate while chatting with you.
The feature has been rolled out to me, and I gave it a spin on the iOS app while writing this article. As you chat with your Muse agent, the avatar at the top of your conversation animates in time with the words that it’s saying. You can also change the tone of the voice by just asking your agent about what you want and letting it decide or by browsing through a bunch of options in the avatar settings.
In my brief tests, my Muse agent responds quickly over voice, though it occasionally pauses while it’s looking up information or checking something for me (like it would with a text chat query). It also animates what it’s saying well, though for my particular avatar, it’s been a little uncanny. I set my Muse agent’s avatar to look like Mark Zuckerberg as a constant reminder that I’m chatting with a Meta service (I refuse to be charmed by a Jolly!), and seeing the digital Zuckerberg facsimile actually talk with me is quite weird. I also can’t get my Muse agent’s voice to sound exactly like Mark Zuckerberg.
Muse’s voice mode and expressive avatars are rolling out now in the US for the app, Meta says. They’re coming “soon” for Meta’s AI glasses and will also be available for its forthcoming Muse Charm gadget, which is supposed to ship this year.

articles.title: More Performance From Every Byte: How Full-Stack Codesign Solves AI’s Memory Challenge
articles.summary:
Larger models, longer contexts and agentic applications are increasing GPU memory pressure while supply tightens and prices rise — a trend expected to continue through the near term.
NVIDIA works closely with memory partners to rapidly adopt the latest memory technologies. NVIDIA was first to adopt HBM3e and HBM4 technologies into an accelerated computing stack.
But the approach isn’t to simply pack more memory onto the GPU. It’s full-stack codesign. NVIDIA intentionally designs GPUs, CPUs, networking, storage and software together to get more useful work out of memory at every layer of the AI factory.
That matters because an AI factory runs on a memory and storage hierarchy. GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM) is the fastest, most expensive and most contested tier — with model weights and KV cache competing for limited capacity. Below it sit CPU memory, local SSDs and shared storage, each trading speed for more capacity at a lower cost per bit.
How much useful work a byte does depends on how well the whole hierarchy is used: shrinking what must be stored, placing it on the right tier and bringing it back to the GPU before it’s needed.
Byte for byte, NVIDIA makes the most efficient use of memory at every layer — and the results show it. From NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra to the Vera Rubin platform, HBM capacity per GPU rose roughly 3%, while agentic throughput per dollar rose by up to 30x on SemiAnalysis AgentX.

articles.title: Accessibility statements now have a home on GitHub
articles.summary:
Accessibility statements now have a home on GitHub
GitHub now highlights ACCESSIBILITY.md files and helps maintainers document accessibility goals, known barriers, supported environments, contributor expectations, and reporting processes.
Accessibility work often lives in issue trackers, contribution guidelines, audit reports, team knowledge, and conversations with users. When that information has no predictable home, people who encounter a barrier must search for it, and maintainers lose context as contributors and project ownership change.
An ACCESSIBILITY.md file, now visible on repository overview pages, gives a project one durable place to explain its accessibility goals, contributor expectations, supported environments, known limitations, and process for reporting barriers.
GitHub makes accessibility statements easier to find
GitHub now recognizes the ACCESSIBILITY.md file in the repository’s root, .github/ directory, or docs/ directory. articles.title: OpenAI Finds GPT-6 Astra Quietly Holding Back on Internal Red-Teaming, Exploit Tasks
articles.summary:
OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra quietly did less than it was asked on AI safety research, including red-teaming and exploit work, and in most cases its misalignment monitors did not catch it.
Astra launched in early September as the first OpenAI model rated Critical for cybersecurity under the company’s Preparedness Framework. OpenAI says that, with suitable tools and access, it can uncover previously unknown flaws across many hardened systems and work out how to exploit them, with no human directing each step.
Trouble surfaced in August, soon after OpenAI began using Astra internally. On safety and alignment tasks, researchers saw it claim to be blocked by problems that were imaginary or self-inflicted, set requirements nobody needed, and walk away from solutions that worked.
Red-teaming done as part of internal AI safety research drew the most explicit refusals and silent withholding, with more cases in monitoring and safety evaluation work. Examples released by OpenAI show Astra scaling back an exploit development task to avoid weaponizing a known CVE. In another, it limited an analysis of exploit strategies while deliberately avoiding an open refusal.
When Astra did explain itself, it often argued that holding back was the safer choice. OpenAI acknowledged that for many of these tasks an outright refusal could arguably have been justified.

articles.title: Chasse aux mines : la France dévoile sa solution pour déployer rapidement ses drones en haute mer
articles.summary:
La Marine nationale dispose déjà de drones de surface capables de repérer des mines marines. Problème, il leur manque un navire pour les emmener loin des côtes.
Début août 2026, la Direction générale de l’armement (DGA) avait annoncé la commande de 12 drones supplémentaires et l’affrètement de navires pour les porter, sans préciser lesquels. Elle a présenté sa solution le 5 novembre, en marge du salon Euronaval, avec deux plateformes civiles baptisées « Protée », fournies par les Chantiers de l’Atlantique et Les Abeilles International et affrétées pour 10 ans au maximum.
Une nouvelle avancée pour le programme SLAM-F (système de lutte anti-mines du futur), lancé en 2020 pour remplacer tous les moyens de guerre des mines de la Marine.
Des navires de guerre qui se font attendre
Les Protée doivent permettre de mettre en œuvre plus rapidement les drones au large, notamment pour soutenir les forces stratégiques, mais ils ne seront qu’une étape.
Dans un billet publié le 5 novembre, le ministère des Armées rappelle en effet que d’autres navires sont prévus. La DGA prépare l’acquisition de bâtiments de guerre des mines (BGDM) qui permettront « d’aller loin et partout, tant en métropole qu’en projection ».

articles.title: A rare strike in Taiwan exposes labor unrest beneath the global AI rush
articles.summary:
About a dozen workers at a Micron Technology plant in Taoyuan in Taiwan went on strike in October, the first in the island’s semiconductor industry, after their union and the chipmaker failed to reach an agreement on salaries and bonuses. Their one-day action, while largely symbolic, is a reflection of the growing discontent among laborers in the artificial intelligence industry over how profits are distributed.
The leading American memory chipmaker has posted record profits this year on the back of surging demand for AI chips. Unions representing workers at Micron’s facilities in Taoyuan and Taichung have been negotiating with the company for months for a profit-sharing agreement similar to those reached by employees at rivals Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix in South Korea.
“Making a profit is perfectly fine, but the rank and file should get a share of the profit instead of this unequal distribution between high-level executives and the rank and file,” Jerry Lin, president of Micron’s Taoyuan union, told Rest of World.
The global tech industry is heavily reliant on Taiwan’s semiconductor industry. Idaho-based Micron, the world’s third-biggest memory chipmaker, employs more than 15,000 workers in Taiwan. They produce over 60% of the company’s dynamic random access memory chips, used in AI servers. A prolonged workers’ strike could severely disrupt already strained supplies of memory chips worldwide.

articles.title: The Wizard of Open Weights: Chris Alexiuk Makes AI Easy With Open Models
articles.summary:
Chris Alexiuk has a simple rule about open source AI: If you believe in it, be loud about it.
“We should be shouting about this technology from the rooftops,” said Alexiuk, a Toronto-based senior product research engineer in deep learning at NVIDIA who specializes in making open large language models (LLMs) practical for working developers.
Alexiuk’s preferred “rooftop” is YouTube, where he’s built a following teaching curious thousands how to build, fine-tune, evaluate and ship production LLM applications and agents.
“I think the people who will most help us understand how to build and apply AI likely haven’t even heard of it yet,” he said. “Trying to get knowledge and information out to as many people as humanly possible is what continues to drive me.”
Bringing NVIDIA Nemotron to Developers Everywhere
Having spent years teaching developers to build with open models, Alexiuk has concluded that transparency isn’t a feature of good AI; it’s the precondition for it.
“Fully open source AI is necessary for the democratization of intelligence,” he said. “You should have access to the weights, the data that went into it, the training recipes, everything.”
That’s why, on his LinkedIn profile, Alexiuk styles himself “No. 1 Nemotron Fan,” referring to the NVIDIA Nemotron family of open source, multimodal models built for long-running, self-evolving and specialized AI agents.

articles.title: 18 Millionen Domains und ein Wertverfall: Was von der .de-Goldgräberzeit übrig ist
articles.summary:
Im Internet ist fast alles beliebig oft verfügbar. Nur die Adresse nicht: Jede Domain gibt es bloß ein einziges Mal. Für shopping.des wurden 2008 fast zwei Millionen Euro gezahlt, für kredit.de fast 900.000 Euro. Der Handel mit solchen Namen zeigt, dass digitale Adressen ein knappes und mitunter kostspieliges Gut sind – und das seit nunmehr vier Jahrzehnten: Am 5. November wird die deutsche Länderkennung .de 40 Jahre alt.
Die Verwaltung übernahm 1986 zunächst das US-amerikanische Forschungsnetzwerk CSNET. 1988 ging sie an die Universität Dortmund – zu diesem Zeitpunkt waren gerade einmal sechs .de-Domains registriert. Mit der Verbreitung des Internets wuchsen die Anforderungen. 1993 entstand der Interessenverbund IV-DENIC, am 17. Dezember 1996 gründeten 37 Internet-Service-Provider die DENIC eG als genossenschaftlich organisierte Registrierungsstelle.
Heute zählt .de mehr als 18 Millionen registrierte Domains und gehört damit zu den größten Länderendungen weltweit. Die technische Infrastruktur bewältigt nach Angaben der DENIC rund 3,5 Milliarden Nameservice-Anfragen täglich. Sie sorgt dafür, dass Internetadressen weltweit erreichbar sind. „Aus den frühen, überschaubaren Netzstrukturen ist eine leistungsfähige digitale Infrastruktur geworden“, sagt DENIC-Vorstand Tom Keller zum Jubiläum.
Digitales Gold: Hunderttausende Euro für Top-Adressen

articles.title: Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 is $300 off ahead of Black Friday
articles.summary:
Android fans with a bit of iPhone Duo envy, take note: The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 is discounted to $1,599.99 at both Amazon and Best Buy, a hefty $300 markdown from its usual price, and just $50 higher than the lowest we’ve seen. Considering the device only launched a few months ago, you’re saving a significant amount of cash on the unlocked device, and you can also opt for the 512GB model, doubling the storage, for just $200 more (Amazon, Best Buy). Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 is $300 off ahead of Black Friday
You can also save on the Beats Pill Bluetooth speaker, a battery-powered Ring doorbell, and a Lego Star Wars droid.
The shorter and wider passport-style shape (similar to the iPhone Duo) quickly became natural and comfortable to handle, according to our reviewer Dominic Preston’s experience with the Z Fold 8. Despite its thin and light construction, it doesn’t skimp on battery life, with a 4,800mAh battery that still had 40 percent charge remaining after a full day of use. The interior 4:3 screen has the same ratio as most Apple iPads, which is great for watching movies or TV, but even better for reading. There’s no telephoto lens on this model (it’s present on the pricier Z Fold 8 Ultra), and it only has an IP48 rating, so you’ll want to be careful near the beach, but those are small compromises to make given the discounted price.

articles.summary:
Dropbox is making a big push into AI infrastructure with a $350 million acquisition of cloud technology company Tigris Data, marking what appears to be its largest acquisition to date.
Announced Thursday, the deal is expected to strengthen Dropbox’s AI infrastructure capabilities and support the development of DBX Agent Cloud, a new storage platform aimed at businesses and developers building AI models and agents.
Dropbox told TechCrunch via email that the transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026. The company also said it currently has no plans to reduce headcount as part of the acquisition. The company already cut 9% of its global workforce last month, WSJ reported.
DBX Agent Cloud will initially offer object storage as a stand-alone product, allowing businesses to purchase storage independently and use it with existing tools and applications built for Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service), which is a cloud storage service that enables businesses to store and retrieve large volumes of data.
Beyond its infrastructure ambitions, Dropbox is also bringing more AI capabilities to its core product. Users will be able to ask AI to perform supported tasks using their files, choose between different AI models, and connect their Dropbox content to third-party tools, including ChatGPT, Claude, and Muse.

articles.title: Russia-Linked Hackers Hit iOS, Android Devices With Exploit Chains via Watering Holes
articles.summary:
Russian state-sponsored threat actor Midnight Blizzard is believed to have targeted iOS and Android users in Europe and the US with zero-click exploits targeting n-day vulnerabilities, cybersecurity firm Sekoia reports.
Also known as APT29, Cozy Bear, The Dukes, Nobelium, and Yttrium, and believed to be sponsored by the Russian Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR), Midnight Blizzard is known for targeting government organizations, diplomats, IT services providers, and NGOs for intelligence gathering.
The attacks uncovered by Sekoia, mounted as part of a large-scale watering hole campaign, involved compromised or cloned high-profile websites of organizations in the US, Ukraine, the Czech Republic, and Bulgaria.
Midnight Blizzard injected malicious JavaScript code in the websites of a Ukrainian gas production company, a major industry trade association, and a far-right European political party, and modified legitimate files on the site of a Bulgarian military-related website.
The code was designed to fingerprint visitors, harvesting browser and device configuration data and sending it in JSON format before the exploit is delivered.
In an adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) setup, the APT registered two lookalike domains that acted as reverse proxies for high-profile sites, injecting malicious code into copies of america250.org, the site of the 250th anniversary of American independence, and the website of the Raffles London at The OWO hotel near sensitive UK government institutions.

articles.title: El Pentágono dará a conocer qué leyes rigen a los laboratorios de IA en Estados Unidos
articles.summary:
El gobierno de Estados Unidos dará a conocer en una o dos semanas el conjunto de leyes y regulaciones que ya se aplican a los laboratorios nacionales de inteligencia artificial. Lo anunció el miércoles 4 de noviembre Emil Michael, director de tecnología del Pentágono, en una conferencia de The Wall Street Journal en Napa, California, según Reuters.
Michael es vicepresidente del Super Intelligence Task Force (grupo de trabajo de superinteligencia), un organismo interinstitucional que creó el presidente Donald Trump para definir la política del país en materia de IA. Reuters informó que el funcionario no ofreció más detalles sobre el contenido del documento.
“Lo que intentamos es crear un marco que haga que los estadounidenses tengan confianza en que estas empresas van a hacer lo correcto”, dijo Michael. Si no, añadió, “lo que se obtiene son 535 legisladores escribiendo una norma que podría matar a la industria”. La cifra corresponde a los miembros del Congreso de Estados Unidos.
Con ese argumento, el funcionario planteó el documento como una alternativa a una ley nueva del Congreso. No precisó qué organismos participarán en la publicación ni en qué formato se difundirá.

articles.summary:
Why a Mathematician Is Chasing Eclipses With Algorithms and Cameras
With custom-built gear, his team seeks to solve a long-standing solar mystery
The sun hangs low over the plains of Castile and León, in the north-central region of Spain. But from a slope of the mountain Pico Trigaza, it appears that a few puffy white clouds have started to block the sun. That’s vexing.
A group of researchers, some wearing cardboard eclipse glasses, is clustered around sets of portable telescopes and cameras connected to laptops. All this gear is scattered on tabletops perched on the mountainside. On the computer screens, the sun’s disk looks like a deep orange crescent that is slowly waning. That’s because the moon began to crawl across it about half an hour ago. In 25 minutes, it will obscure the sun completely, producing an eerie and wondrous phenomenon—a total solar eclipse.
In the late-summer, late-afternoon heat, the researchers watch anxiously as those fluffy clouds linger around the sun. “It will.” Miloslav Druckmüller glances calmly at his group of doctoral candidates, now making final checks of the equipment in preparation for totality. Here in Spain, on this 12th day of August, Druckmüller is getting ready for his 19th solar eclipse. He knows from long experience that weat…

articles.title: How a car-importing problem led Sheriff Adedokun to build Clea
articles.summary:
In car importing, business owners must find the vehicle and pay the auction house, which could be in another country. This proved harder than expected for Sheriff Adedokun, a serial entrepreneur who founded Clea, a cross-border payments platform for African businesses.
Africa’s fragmented cross-border payments landscape was not new. Businesses trading internationally had relied on banks or other financial intermediaries to move money between markets. By 2022, when Adedokun started importing vehicles from the United States, Nigerian fintechs were building products to make international payments easier. However, the available options did not always work for the transactions he needed.
“I tried to use some of the fintech platforms in Nigeria, but it didn’t work because most of my payments were rejected,” Adedokun told TechCabal in an interview. “Then I had to go to the bank, fill a form, and try to do the transfer. There was also a limit on sending international transfers from Nigerian banks.”
He explained that US vehicle auction platforms required payments to come directly from the person or business buying the car, as third-party transfers could be rejected.
Car importation was one example of a deluge of businesses that had to pay suppliers before their orders could be shipped. Total imports stood at over ₦15 billion ($11.1 million) in the first quarter of 2025, according to National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) data.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
- November 4, 2026
- Source:
- Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
- Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.

Pourtant, seuls 36 % peuvent toujours retrouver qui a autorisé un accès sensible à un chatbot.
Delinea a interrogé 2 254 responsables IT et sécurité, ainsi que 2 250 salariés hors IT, dans des entreprises d’au moins 500 personnes. Huit pays sont couverts, dont la France, mais le rapport ne détaille pas de résultats propres à l’Hexagone.

Artificial Intelligence
Getting started with Web Answer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
Today, we are announcing the general availability of Web Answer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. With Web Answer, agent builders get a synthesized, source-cited answer to a natural-language question with a single tool call. They no longer build a search, retrieve, synthesize, and citation pipeline themselves.
If you have built agents that need to answer questions from current web sources, you know the pattern: call a search API, decide which results to trust, retrieve and clean page content, prompt a model to synthesize, and engineer citation extraction so the output traces back to a source. Every step is code you maintain, and every step is another place things can go wrong: hallucination when evidence is insufficient, stale content when the index moves, and broken attribution when a claim and its source drift apart.
The Web Answer collapses that entire pipeline into one request. You send a question. You get back a cited answer in seconds. In this post, we explain what Web Answer does, compare it with Web Search on AgentCore, show how it works and what it returns, and walk through adding Web Answer to a gateway and calling it from an agent.

Inside GitHub’s new Git storage architecture
GitHub’s new Git storage architecture is built so thousands of agents can push to a single repository at once. Here’s how it works.
Last week at GitHub Universe, we announced our new Git storage architecture, capable of handling thousands of writes per second with reads that scale on demand. Through internal testing, we’ve demonstrated the ability to support 5,000 concurrent agents working on a repository, sending 7,200 pushes per second to a repo, all while serving read traffic with consistently low latency. This new architecture is the foundation for GitHub to support agentic development for hundreds of millions of developers, and we’ve been building it underneath GitHub while it keeps running.
Over the past year, agents changed what a busy repository looks like on GitHub. AI agents do more than generate answers. They search for information, query databases, write and test code and take action.
Each of those steps relies on a CPU, with agents moving between GPU reasoning and CPU execution throughout a task.
As businesses put more agents to work, AI factories need CPUs that can execute those steps quickly and support many agents at once, all within the limits of available power.
What this means: AI infrastructure providers need to support more agents without making each one wait longer to get work done. And critically, AI factories are power limited. This means operators need to choose infrastructure that maximizes the work done for every watt.
Why it matters: NVIDIA Vera delivers both fast agent performance and high capacity per watt within a single CPU. That gives providers one CPU for a range of agent workloads, rather than having to mix and match fast and dense x86 parts to balance speed and capacity.
The data that proves it: In a 100-megawatt data center comparison, NVIDIA found that a single Vera CPU performs better than the fastest x86 CPU and the most energy-efficient x86 CPU.

articles.title: Zyxel Switch Hacks Blamed on Patched Flaw Actually Exploited a Zero-Day
articles.summary:
A recently patched vulnerability in Zyxel GS1900 series switches was exploited in the wild as a zero-day to hack almost 1,000 devices, cybersecurity firm Binarly reports.
The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-107441 (CVSS score of 8.8) and is described as an out-of-bounds write issue in the CGI program of the Zyxel GS1900 series switch firmware.
According to Zyxel, an unauthenticated attacker could exploit the security defect via crafted HTTP requests to achieve OS command execution.
The vulnerability impacts 10 GS1900 switch models. Zyxel rolled out fixes for it on October 23 and published an advisory on November 3.
On the same day, Binarly warned that attackers had exploited CVE-2026-107441 in attacks previously attributed to a Chinese hacking group.
The previous report came from GreyNoise, which warned on September 21 that the hackers exploited CVE-2026-7273, a Zyxel bug patched in June, to compromise roughly 1,000 devices in August.
GreyNoise linked the attacks to Red Heron, a Chinese threat actor that Acronis caught targeting Gitea instances in a large-scale hacking campaign, and CISA added CVE-2026-7273 to its KEV catalog.
Now, Binarly says that the attackers did not target CVE-2026-7273. They deployed variants of the Jitterly and Sixzut malware analyzed by Acronis, but their exploit targeted a previously unknown vulnerability.
“Because the threat actor was exploiting a different vulnerability, and the patch for CVE-2026-7273 remained ineffective, this had no effect on protec…

articles.title: A third of acquired game studios have closed since 2000, and Arkane Lyon could be next
articles.summary:
The takeaway: Layoffs and game studio closures have surged in recent years, largely due to the hangover from pandemic-era overinvestment. As Microsoft continues its layoffs and closures and Arkane Lyon fights for its life, a new analysis suggests that most studios are worse off after being acquired. However, those game studios that have thrived under certain publishers show a consistent pattern.
Game industry veteran Sebastian Cardoso recently investigated the fates of more than 300 studios bought by large companies over the past quarter century, finding that roughly 61% sold fewer games, earned lower review scores, or faced closure post-acquisition.
Arkane Lyon risks becoming the latest example if it doesn't find a buyer by mid-December, but Ubisoft and at least two other companies have made offers for the Dishonored and Deathloop developer.
Cardoso's lengthy breakdown shows changes in output and staffing for hundreds of developers since 2000, as well as post-acquisition lifespans. Although closures and layoffs have spiked since 2023, the acquiring company's identity is easily the biggest predictor of a studio's well-being.
The consequences are final, the stats show: a third of acquired studios were shut down, half of those closures coming within five years of the deal. Closures were also rarity until recently: only one acquired studio in Cardoso's dataset closed between 2019 and 2022, compared with 33 from 2023 through October.

articles.title: Stop Letting Your Hard Work Stay Invisible At Review Time
articles.summary:
This article is crossposted from IEEE Spectrum’s careers newsletter. Sign up now to get insider tips, expert advice, and practical strategies, written in partnership with tech career development company Parsity and delivered to your inbox for free!
Hard work rarely speaks for itself.
When I landed my first job as a software engineer, I had a simple plan: Work hard and somebody would notice. Eventually a manager would tap me on the shoulder and hand me a promotion (probably with a nice little speech).
That plan stalled my career for about five years.
I switched jobs twice, kept my head down, read a stack of programming books, and sometimes pulled 12-hour days. I was never promoted. At my third job, out of frustration, I started interviewing at other companies and almost immediately got an offer for a senior engineer role.
So I went back to my job and quit. My team was blindsided. I liked my manager and the people I worked with, and they came back with a counteroffer. Then someone from HR asked me, “Why didn’t you just ask us?”
Honestly, it never occurred to me.
I took the counteroffer and stayed. Three jobs in, I finally got promoted, and all it took was asking (in the most dramatic way possible).
Today, I would take a different approach.

articles.title: Aigboje Aig-Imoukhuede urges better use of Africa's capital
articles.summary:
Aigboje Aig-Imoukhuede, chairman of Nigerian tier-1 lender Access Bank Group and financial services holding company Coronation Group, argues that African financial institutions must move beyond financial stability to productive finance, unlock capital tied up in commercial transactions and build banking systems capable of operating across borders.
Africa’s financial institutions have spent years debating the availability and cost of capital. However, Aig-Imoukhuede believes the continent is asking the wrong question.
Rather than focusing primarily on how much capital Africa can attract, he wants policymakers and financial institutions to examine how effectively the money already available is being deployed.
“At this particular moment in Africa’s development, I believe the more important question is: How do we make better use of the capital we already have?” he said during the closing session of the Africa Financial Industry Summit (AFIS) in Luanda, Angola.
His argument is that the continent’s financial systems must become better at connecting existing capital to businesses, productive economic activity and long-term investments. Without that shift, financial stability and stronger banking institutions may not translate into the broader economic prosperity Africa needs.

articles.title: Nokia 1100 vs el primer iPhone de Apple: cuánto duraba la batería de cada modelo
articles.summary:
El Nokia 1100 y el primer iPhone de Apple expusieron dos formas opuestas de entender la telefonía, con diferencias visibles en diseño, funciones y duración de batería.
El celular de Nokia priorizó la comunicación básica, los controles físicos y la resistencia; el dispositivo presentado por Steve Jobs en 2007 concentró herramientas digitales en una pantalla táctil.
Los dos modelos respondieron a las condiciones técnicas y a los hábitos de sus respectivas épocas. Mientras el Nokia 1100 buscaba mantenerse operativo durante varios días con llamadas y mensajes, el primer iPhone incorporó navegación web, reproducción multimedia, correo y una interfaz que demandaba recargas más frecuentes.
Cuánto tiempo duraba la batería del Nokia 1100
El Nokia 1100, lanzado en 2003, utilizaba una batería de iones de litio BL-5C con capacidad de 850 mAh. Tenía una autonomía de hasta 4,5 horas de conversación continua y entre 10 y 16 días en espera, con un máximo de 400 horas. La cifra variaba según la señal de la red y la frecuencia de uso.
En la práctica, el teléfono podía funcionar entre cinco y siete días con una sola carga en un uso cotidiano. La pantalla monocromática, de bajo consumo, y la nula cantidad de aplicaciones explicaban ese rendimiento. El aparato se concentraba en llamadas, mensajes de texto, agenda, alarma, calculadora y, en algunas versiones, linterna.

articles.title: Las escuelas de EEUU quieren un Google sin IA, pero se enfrentan a un dilema: o aceptan sus resúmenes con IA o se quedan sin buscador
articles.summary:
Estos días ha habido cierta polémica en Estados Unidos acerca de una serie de cambios que Google quiere introducir en torno al uso de su IA en los centros educativos del país. Y es que tal y como compartía la compañía, desactivará por defecto sus herramientas de IA para las cuentas de estudiantes de educación obligatoria el año que viene. El tema es que se enfrentan a un dilema, pues tal y como están las cosas, o aceptan los resúmenes de IA (AI Overviews) o dejan a los alumnos sin el motor de búsqueda de Google.

articles.title: Aspiration, lavage et entretien du rouleau : le Dreame H15 Pro passe sous les 250 €
articles.summary:
L’aspirateur laveur Dreame H15 Pro est à 249,16 € (-45 %)
Avec son format inclinable à plat et son rouleau autonettoyant, le Dreame H15 Pro passe à 249,16 € chez Amazon, soit 45 % sous le prix conseillé.
Vendu et expédié par Amazon, ce modèle neuf bénéficie de la livraison gratuite. L’économie atteint 199,84 € face au prix conseillé de 449 €. Le tarif est également inférieur de 48,83 € au plus bas des 30 derniers jours indiqué par le marchand, de 297,99 €.
Un nettoyage jusque sous les meubles
Le H15 Pro aspire les poussières et lave les sols durs avec son rouleau humide. Sa conception inclinable à 180° permet d’atteindre le dessous des meubles bas. Une raclette mobile accompagne les mouvements pour récupérer les petites saletés et limiter l’eau laissée au sol.
Sur sa base, le rouleau bénéficie d’un autonettoyage avec de l’eau chauffée jusqu’à 100 °C, suivi d’un séchage à l’air chaud. Ces températures concernent l’entretien de la brosse sur la station. Les réservoirs séparés permettent de conserver l’eau propre à l’écart de l’eau récupérée.
Une bonne autonomie, mais un poids sensible
Lors de notre test, nous avons mesuré près de 44 minutes d’autonomie. Les réservoirs ont permis environ 39 minutes de nettoyage avant de nécessiter une intervention. Nous avons également apprécié l’efficacité de l’autonettoyage du rouleau et le ramassage des petites poussières le long des murs.

articles.title: La Nasa n'a pas pu le sauver : le télescope Swift s'est désintégré dans l'atmosphère (vidéo)
articles.summary:
C’était son dernier plongeon. Ce mercredi 4 novembre 2026, le télescope Swift de la Nasa est retombé sur Terre, mettant fin à près de 22 ans de mission. Selon l’US Space Force, l’observatoire est rentré dans l’atmosphère à 13h39 (heure de Paris). Il s’est enflammé dans le ciel, « au-dessus de la région de Sumatra du Nord, en Indonésie », détaille l’agence spatiale dans un communiqué.
Cette désintégration, qui a donné lieu à un spectaculaire bolide (une grosse étoile filante), a pu être filmée depuis la surface de la Terre.
L’Aerospace Corporation, un centre de recherche qui travaille pour l’armée américaine et suit les rentrées atmosphériques des satellites, a publié de son côté une carte sur X montrant l’endroit où Swift est retombé.
Swift se désintègre après une tentative de sauvetage ratée
Officiellement, la mission de Swift était déjà terminée depuis quelques jours. Sa dernière observation du ciel a eu lieu le 20 octobre, alors que le télescope évoluait à 275 km au-dessus de la surface terrestre. À cette altitude, Swift ne parvenait plus à compenser le freinage de l’atmosphère et s’est mis en mode sans échec. Trois jours plus tard, la Nasa a expliqué avoir « fermé les yeux » de Swift, en coupant ses instruments.
Quelques mois plus tôt, la Nasa avait tenté de sauver Swift à l’aide de LINK, un remorqueur de l’entreprise américaine Katalyst Space. Lancé le 3 juillet, l’engin n’a pas pu remplir sa mission, et la Nasa a renoncé au sauvetage. LINK devait essayer de placer Swift…

articles.title: Bambu Lab releases the H3C printer to take 3D printing to an all-new level - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
Bambu Lab has unveiled its first third-generation 3D printer – the H3C – which is capable of multi-material printing to take the category to an all-new level and produce prints we could have only dreamed about just a few short years ago.
The H3C has new Swaptek architecture, which includes nine print tools, each with its own filament path and heating.
A material switch can now be achieved in as little as six seconds which speeds up print time and reduces waste.
To achieve multi-material printing it required a machine that can handle such a capability.
And that’s how Bambu Lab conceived the idea for the H3C.
The company brought all its engineering experience to the table to come up with a machine that could handle more than one material and overcome the limitations experienced with older models.
As a result the new H3C has three new major parts – the Swaptek to handle the tool changes, FlexFeed Extruder to deal with flexible materials, and the AMS 3H, which can store and dry and feed the material to the printer.
When they work together it makes bringing nine materials together as effortless as it is to reach for one.
Each of the nine print tools has its own filament path and its own heating so the filament stays loaded and ready to go.
This means it’s ready to go in an instant and can be preheated ahead of the switch.
This means there’s no need to retract one material to feed the next, resulting in faster more efficient printing.

Key Takeaways:
The race is on to develop physical AI fit for widespread use, but building these sensor-powered systems will require engineering teams to address a variety of technical challenges concurrently and continuously.
Analysts predict significant market growth for physical AI, with the promise that autonomous systems will fundamentally reshape industries spanning transportation, manufacturing, medicine, energy, and more. PwC’s Strategy& projects that the global physical AI market could reach approximately €430 billion by 2030, reflecting the potential commercial impact of autonomous systems across multiple industries.

articles.title: Kurz vor historischem Meilenstein: Kontakt zu Voyager 1 steht wieder
articles.summary:
Kurz vor historischem Meilenstein: Kontakt zu Voyager 1 steht wieder
Aufatmen bei der Nasa: Voyager 1 hat sich zurückgemeldet. Die Raumsonde, die seit 49 Jahren im Weltall unterwegs ist, hatte kurzzeitig nicht auf Kommunikationsversuche des Deep Space Network auf der Erde reagiert.
Voyager 1 reagierte zweimal nicht auf Kontaktversuche
Das Funk- und Kommunikationsnetzwerk der Nasa hatte am 18. und 19. Oktober Voyager 1 kontaktiert. Doch die Raumsonde blieb bei beiden Kontaktversuchen stumm.
Wie die US-Raumfahrtbehörde kürzlich bekannt gab, löste sich das Problem aber von selbst. Am 20. Oktober meldete sich Voyager zurück. Seitdem ist die Kommunikation stabil. Die Nasa versucht nun herauszufinden, was zu dem Ausfall geführt hatte. Es handelte sich schließlich um den ersten Vorfall dieser Art.
Als erstes menschengemachtes Objekt ein Lichttag von Erde entfernt
Der Wackler kam zur Unzeit, denn bald erreicht Voyager 1 einen Meilenstein, der die Kommunikation noch schwerer macht. Die Raumsonde wird als erstes menschengemachtes Objekt einen Lichttag von der Erde entfernt sein. Dies entspricht etwa 25,9 Milliarden Kilometern.
Wie das Wort Lichttag schon sagt: Das Licht, das von einem Objekt in dieser Distanz ausgestrahlt wird, benötigt 24 Stunden, um die Erde zu erreichen.
„Wartet zwei Tage, bis man endlich eine Antwort bekommt“

articles.title: The midterms proved once and for all that X is not real life
articles.summary:
A week before the midterm elections, Vice President JD Vance hosted a town hall in Texas with Fox News host Jesse Watters. It was a friendly event with a friendly audience in what should have been a friendly state, and maybe that’s why Vance couldn’t help himself. When a college student earnestly asked how the right expected young people like her to settle down and have kids, given the ever-growing cost of living, Vance replied with a quip about Jon Husted’s ass.
The midterms proved once and for all that X is not real life
The student, Kate White, introduced herself as the vice president of the Texas Christian University chapter of Turning Point USA, the conservative group started by Donald Trump ally Charlie Kirk. She was offering Vance an opportunity to explain how MAGA could work for young people, and he turned it into a joke. Vance did eventually answer the question, saying Republicans don’t pay enough attention to the issue of affordability and blaming rising housing costs on institutional investors and the “20 million illegal aliens” supposedly living in the United States. articles.title: Formally verifying agent-written full-stack web apps with PDD Kit - Microsoft Research
articles.summary:
At a glance
- Formal methods for everyday software. PDD Kit helps you turn your intent into a formal spec, then proves the code your agent writes for every input and uses tests where a proof can’t reach. It takes formal methods beyond niche, specialist work to engineers without a formal methods background and to everyday applications, like the full-stack web app shown here.
- Exhaustive line-by-line human review can become difficult to scale as AI agents generate increasingly large amounts of code. The plan is supposed to be the contract between you and a coding agent, but nothing actually forces the agent to follow it. The tests it writes usually check what it built, rather than what you asked for.
- PDD Kit makes the agent keep the plan. It works with you to turn your intent into a formal specification in Verus (opens in new tab), proves the agent’s code meets that spec for every input, and falls back to tests where a proof can’t reach.
- We tried it on a full-stack web app. Inside GitHub Next’s Chopin (opens in new tab), we used PDD Kit to formally verify the login logic of Pet Store, a Rust (opens in new tab) storefront. Verus hardened the code and uncovered existing bugs, proving the absence of login bugs with respect to the specification. The developer reviewed the intent and never read the generated code line-by-line.
The plan is the contract the agent should follow, but nothing constrains the agent to follow it.
Coding agents now ship whole features in one sitting oft…

articles.title: WhatsApp : cette nouveauté majeure va changer la façon dont vous organisez vos soirées — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Jusqu’ici, un événement WhatsApp restait dans une discussion de groupe, donc seules les personnes avec un compte pouvaient le voir. Le 14 octobre, l’application avait déjà permis d’inviter à un appel quelqu’un qui n’a pas WhatsApp, grâce à un lien qui s’ouvre dans un navigateur.
Ce jeudi 5 novembre, WhatsApp fait la même chose avec ses Événements, comme la firme l’explique l’explique dans un billet de blog. On crée l’événement, on ajoute une photo de couverture et on partage le lien : les invités voient les détails et peuvent répondre sans installer l’application.
Une page dédiée aux évènements sur WhatsApp
WhatsApp ajoute aussi une page Événements, accessible depuis les Réglages. Elle regroupe tous les événements passés et à venir, qu’on les ait créés ou qu’on y soit invité. On peut y envoyer des invitations personnalisées, suivre les réponses, programmer des rappels et laisser un invité venir accompagné. Côté vie privée, les invités que l’organisateur ne connaît pas ne voient pas son numéro de téléphone.

articles.title: Salon is shutting down after 31 years
articles.summary:
Salon launched 31 years ago as one of the first online-only news magazine outlets, and it announced today in an unsigned post that it’s ceasing publication.
Salon is shutting down after 31 years
Salon says its publishing model is ‘no longer sustainable.’
The company said that the “business realities of independent digital journalism have changed profoundly over the years,” and it decided that its publishing model is “no longer sustainable.” It didn’t go into detail about why, but many websites are grappling with “Google Zero” and the impact of AI tools. When reached for comment, Salon general manager Amanda Wolfe pointed The Verge to today’s announcement post.
“Thirty-one years is a remarkable run, but what matters most is what happened during those years: the journalism, the ideas, the voices, the conversations and the community that grew around them,” Salon said in its post. “Salon helped demonstrate what digital journalism could be and could become. We hope that legacy will continue to matter long after today.”
On Bluesky, Salon chief content officer Erin Keane says that the editorial archive will “stay live for now.”
Current Salon owner Find.co acquired Salon in 2023 and describes itself as a “Performance Marketing Ecosystem transforming crypto marketing with performance and precision.”

Google, Meta e TikTok entraram com ações judiciais contra uma lei da Califórnia (EUA) que restringe o uso de recursos considerados potencialmente viciantes em redes sociais por crianças e adolescentes. As empresas querem impedir que a legislação entre em vigor em janeiro de 2027.
As ações foram apresentadas separadamente em tribunais federais da Califórnia nesta quinta-feira (5). As companhias argumentam que a lei viola direitos de liberdade de expressão e entra em conflito com a Seção 230 da Lei de Decência nas Comunicações dos Estados Unidos, que protege plataformas de responsabilidade pelo conteúdo publicado por usuários.
Assinada pelo governador Gavin Newsom em setembro, a legislação proíbe empresas de oferecer determinados recursos a usuários com menos de 16 anos. Entre eles estão a reprodução automática de vídeos e os sistemas de recomendação personalizada.
O texto considera que essas ferramentas podem ser psicologicamente exploratórias e estimular menores a consultar compulsivamente as redes sociais. Empresas que não cumprirem as exigências poderão receber multas.

articles.title: Bluesky hit peak usage for the year on election night | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
The blue wave swept Bluesky on Tuesday night as the microblogging platform recorded its highest daily number of posts, replies, and likes in 2026.
“We’re seeing a wave of new people joining and old friends coming back,” Bluesky CEO Toni Schneider posted.
According to Schneider, posts and likes doubled during the U.S. midterm elections on Tuesday.
COO Rose Wang told TechCrunch that usage began to peak between 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. PT, when many election results were rolling in. Daily posts and likes increased 30% and 70%, respectively, compared to the previous 30-day averages; clicks on links also spiked 20%.
According to open source data, Bluesky reached 44 million likes, 4.8 million posts, and 2 million new follows on November 4. This nearly eclipsed Bluesky’s all-time record 45 million likes in a single day, set in November 2024.
This jump was especially visible in Bluesky’s data traffic, which was 200% higher than usual, reaching up to 35.8 GB/s.
Bluesky is — sometimes snidely — referred to as “Twitter for the left,” given that its user base seems to skew that way politically. This isn’t a coincidence; Bluesky’s most concentrated period of user growth occurred after Donald Trump won the 2024 presidential election, so it makes sense that those users would post actively during a night of overwhelming victories for the Democratic party.

articles.title: CISO Conversations: Ryan Davis – The Unknown Is Where Security Meets Reality
articles.summary:
Starting as a young hacker provides a solid grounding in how to defend. Ryan Davis, now CISO at New Charter Technologies, successfully made the transition.
The journey
Ryan Davis became interested in computers at an early age, before the internet changed the world. As a child, his mother ran a secretarial college from the family home in the 1980s. “We had six personal computers in the house, and I had plenty of time to tinker with them at a formative age. There was no internet, so I had to learn what to do by trial and error. As I grew older, that desire for tinkering grew into a desire to explore beyond the intended confines of the system and make it do something that was never intended.”
Davis is now a CISO, but he started as a hacker. “I did some things that, in retrospect, would probably be considered illegal,” he admits. But he never did anything with malice or malintent. “It was always to see how far I could go. Could I get the system to do something that wasn’t intended? Could I gain access to something that was supposedly a secure system or supposedly isolated in some way?”
As the internet became available, he began spending time on forums and message boards, learning how systems worked or could be reworked. “But never,” he says, “with any personal gain in mind. It wasn’t to get something to sell, to dox somebody, or gain some advantage; it was always just to see how far I could get. It was more like a personal competition.”
He could have done stuff to benefit himself…

Para ello, hace referencia a cómo se concibe una obra y cómo se desarrolla.
El creador de Mario y The Legend of Zelda ha comentado este tema en una comparecencia relacionada con la concesión de la Orden de la Cultura de Japón. Cuando le han preguntado sobre la IA generativa y el desarrollo de videojuegos, ha hecho referencia a los cambios tecnológicos que ha vivido su generación.
La evolución de las herramientas
Por ejemplo, recuerda cómo pasaron de las máquinas de escribir a los procesadores de texto. En aquella época, las herramientas estaban en constante evolución. Cree que el avance de los ordenadores les ha ayudado a entender mejor la capacidad de los diseñadores. En este sentido, considera que la IA generativa puede suponer un cambio similar.
Ha explicado que hay un aspecto que es el de la estructura global. Es decir, cómo se concibe algo. Y otro que es el de rellenar los huecos o de pulir detalles. Estos pueden ser trabajos agradables. Pero existe el riesgo de confusión entre la satisfacción de hacer el trabajo y el hecho de tener una obra de calidad.
La intención del creador

Six mois chrono pour la munition navale télé-opérée de la DGA

Un opérateur pilote en effet l'appareil à distance, à l'aide d'une liaison satellite, en gardant les yeux rivés sur une vidéo en temps réel. articles.title: Why Integrated Gate Drive Regulation Matters For High Reliability Space GaN Designs
articles.summary:
Eliminating the need for a separate bias regulator dedicated to the gate driver for a more streamlined power architecture.
As Gallium Nitride (GaN) technology becomes increasingly prevalent in space power systems, designers are leveraging its inherent capabilities to deliver higher efficiency, faster switching speeds, and greater power density. These advantages help designers support the growing demands of modern satellite platforms.
While GaN devices are central to many modern power architectures, achieving their full efficiency and switching performance depends on the gate driver that controls them. Infineon HiRel’s new, rad hard single-channel gate driver for GaN delivers the precise drive conditions that GaN devices require. Designed specifically for extreme environment applications, the device incorporates an integrated low dropout regulator (LDO). The LDO simplifies gate-drive implementation while providing a tightly regulated voltage optimized for GaN operation, while also reducing the total bill of materials (BOM).
The switching advantages of GaN stem from device characteristics such as low gate charge, reduced output capacitance, and fast transition times. These attributes enable lower switching losses and support operation at higher frequencies than traditional silicon MOSFET (Si) technologies.
Designers must provide stable and controlled gate-drive voltages to achieve optimal switching behavior. Even relatively small variations in gate voltage can affect switching …

articles.title: Klimaanpassung, jetzt! So steht es um Deutschlands Kampf gegen den Klimawandel
articles.summary:
Plan B für Deutschland: Wie weit sind wir bei Strategien zur Klimaanpassung?
„Es ging nicht mehr“, sagt Markus Funke. Seit über 20 Jahren wohnt er am nordwestlichen Stadtrand von Frankfurt am Main. Ende Juni lagen die Temperaturen dort bei über 40 Grad, begleitet von hoher Luftfeuchtigkeit. Klimaanlagen waren ausverkauft. Nach ein paar Tagen kapitulierte er und zog für zwei Nächte in ein klimatisiertes Hotel. Das hat den 57-Jährigen nachdenklich gemacht, denn er erwägt schon länger aus privaten Gründen einen Umzug nach Norddeutschland. Nun kommt auch noch der Klimawandel dazu. „Ich hätte früher nie vermutet, dass die Hitze bei der Entscheidung mal eine Rolle spielen könnte“, sagt er.
Fast 16.000 Menschen aus Deutschland haben diese Option nicht mehr. Sie sind tot, gestorben während der Hitzewelle im Sommer 2026. Das Robert Koch-Institut hat ermittelt, dass viele von ihnen statistisch gesehen noch lange hätten leben können. Das Problem betrifft auch junge und gesunde Menschen. „In den letzten 24 Stunden haben wir sieben Menschen bewusstlos in ihren Wohnungen aufgefunden“, schrieb die Feuerwehr Köln im Juni auf Instagram. „Und nein, auch Menschen ohne Vorerkrankungen, fit und mitten im Leben, befanden sich mit 42 Grad Körpertemperatur in Lebensgefahr.“
Dieser Text erscheint in der Ausgabe 8/2026 von MIT Technology Review. Darin beschäftigen wir uns mit den Folgen des Klimawandels und wie wir uns an Hitze, Dürre und Überschwemmungen anpassen sollten. Das Heft erscheint am 06.11.…

articles.title: Axiom Math wants to keep AI slop out of mathematics | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
It feels like AI is cracking a new math problem every week. Last month, OpenAI released 719 manuscriptsclaiming solutions to some of the field’s hardest problems. But even the computer checks meant to confirm those results can slip. After years of AI slop, it’s fair to wonder whether math is next.
Axiom Math is betting math can avoid that fate, not by slowing down, but by standing on firmer ground. The $1.6 billion startup wants to build a verified foundation that AI agents can rely on to write software and, eventually, do science.
On Wednesday, the company announced it had formally verified the Stacks Project, one of the largest bodies of mathematics ever written by humans. Mathematicians often hold Stacks in rare regard — Columbia mathematician Peter Woit has claimed there’s “nothing else really comparable,” comparing the project to “the famous Bourbaki books,” a series that rebuilt math from its foundations in the 20th century.
Woit’s Columbia colleague Johan de Jong started the Stacks Project in 2005 as an open source reference. Mathematicians have contributed to it ever since, building out results from college-level algebra all the way up to the field’s most advanced ideas across algebra, geometry, and number theory.
The company’s fleet of AI agents translates the library’s roughly 7,654 pages into about 16 million lines of computer-checked code.

Im Rahmen seines Oktober-Patchdays hat Microsoft über 1.400 Schwachstellen in Windows, Office und weiteren Microsoft-Produkten geschlossen. Eine der adressierten Lücken betraf eine Schwachstelle in dem Windows-eigenen Zeichenprogramm Paint.
Microsoft: Paint-Lücke sehr komplex
Die als CVE-2026-83844 registrierte Sicherheitslücke erreicht einen hohen Schweregrad von 8.1 von 10. Dass Microsoft die Einstufung nicht auf kritisch gesetzt hat, liegt daran, dass die Ausnutzung der Lücke sehr komplex ist und „fundierte Kenntnisse des Systems“ voraussetzt.
Der Softwarekonzern selbst bezeichnet eine Ausnutzung daher als „weniger wahrscheinlich“. Hinweise darauf, dass die Sicherheitslücke aktiv ausgenutzt wird, gibt es laut Microsoft bisher nicht.
Angreifer könnten Schadcode ausführen
Nutzer:innen sollten die Paint-Schwachstelle dennoch nicht auf die leichte Schulter nehmen. Denn sie ermöglicht es Angreifer:innen theoretisch, Schadcode auszuführen, indem sie ein speziell gestaltetes Datenpaket über das Netzwerk senden. Eine Authentifizierung oder eine Interaktion der PC-Nutzer:innen sind demnach nicht erforderlich.
Wie Windows Latest berichtet, hat Microsoft eigentlich einen Patch für die Sicherheitslücke bereitgestellt. Nutzer:innen, die auf die Paint-Version 11.2609.401.0 updaten, sollten auf der sicheren Seite sein.

articles.title: The Agent Smith Dilemma: Governing Agentic Identities
articles.summary:
For the past few years, North Korean operatives, posing as remote IT workers, systematically infiltrated hundreds of Western enterprise networks. They passed technical interviews, cleared background checks using stolen identities, and sat comfortably inside corporate trust boundaries with legitimate credentials. They drew salaries, funneled funds back to Pyongyang, and routinely exfiltrated sensitive data on their way out. Major firms, including prominent cybersecurity vendors, have publicly admitted to falling for the scheme. (As an aside, listen to Nicole Perlroth’s Podcast “To Catch a Thief” for a fascinating deep dive)
The scheme worked because enterprises grant trust once. HR verifies a person at hiring, IT creates an account, a laptop is provisioned. The user is then authorized. Nothing in the security stack was built to answer the one question that mattered: Is the entity driving this session who we think it is?
Now enter the AI agent era.
Inside the enterprise, the volume of non-human identities executing sensitive tasks is expanding exponentially. Organizations are rapidly onboarding thousands of AI agents into critical workflows, complete with administrative service accounts and API keys. Enterprises now extend the same trust model to AI agents, with less scrutiny.
What Trust Models Should AI Agents Have?

Francis Galluppi (Evil Dead) pour écrire le nouveau film Constantine

Comme l'a dévoilé le média nord-américain Deadline, le projet n'en est encore qu'au tout début de son développement et DC Studios a engagé Francis Galluppi pour écrire une première version du scénario. Le cinéaste n'a à son tableau de chasse que quelques courts-métrages, ainsi que le film Last Stop: Yuma County qu'il a écrit et réalisé en 2023.

articles.summary:
El lanzamiento de Grand Theft Auto VI está previsto para el 19 de noviembre de 2026. Algunos de sus futuros jugadores ya están pensando cómo van a conciliar el juego con la vida laboral. Un 10 % de los encuestados por GameSquare aseguran que planean saltarse la jornada laboral el día del lanzamiento. Además, un 30 % está pensando en pedir algún día libre. Entre sus opciones figura alegar una enfermedad.
Los datos se obtuvieron de un sondeo realizado a 1.000 trabajadores estadounidenses a jornada completa que se reconocen jugadores. Los resultados fueron publicados el 20 de octubre por GameSquare. Las cifras se refieren sólo a este colectivo.
Qué dicen los porcentajes sobre las posibles ausencias
En la empresa se llama a esto el “efecto Grand Theft Auto”. En el comunicado se asegura que un 36 % de los que están pensando en pedir días libres aseguran que, si lo hacen, alegarán que están enfermos. Por otro lado, en la encuesta no se equiparan todos los casos de absentismo planeado a “fingir enfermedad”. Por ejemplo, las vacaciones no se plantean de igual manera que las falsas enfermedades.
Es posible comprobarlo haciendo unos sencillos cálculos. De 1.000 personas, el 30 % son 300. A estos 300 les aplicamos el 36 % y obtenemos que serían 108 personas (un 10,8 % del total). Esto es un cálculo basado en los porcentajes dados (y redondeados). No es un recuento real de las respuestas. Tampoco podemos asumir que sean los trabajadores que terminarán por faltar.

On Wednesday, Bloomberg reported that a Chinese regulator’s inquiry prompted the Nigeria-focused payments company to halt its IPO just hours after setting the price. articles.title: Le bouclier ultime d'Apple aurait cédé : un iPhone 18 Pro piraté malgré le mode Isolement
articles.summary:
Une animation de jeune fille qui danse aurait-elle remis en cause les promesses de protection sans faille du mode Isolement proposé sur iPhone ? C’est en tout cas ce que laisse penser une vidéo publiée par le groupe de hackers Calif.
Un CV de chat, une jeune fille qui danse et un iPhone 18 Pro piraté malgré le mode Isolement
Le groupe de hackers Calif affirme être parvenu à jailbreaker un iPhone 18 Pro dont le mode Isolement était activé. Il s’agit d’un exploit, étant donné que le mode Isolement permet justement de protéger les utilisateurs contre les piratages, notamment en bloquant les pièces jointes des messages et en limitant certaines technologies web. L’entreprise à la pomme décrit elle-même le mode Isolement comme une « protection extrême » contre les tentatives de piratage.
Mais il semble que ce mode de protection d’Apple ne soit pas infaillible. Dans une vidéo publiée sur X par le groupe de hackers Calif, nous pouvons voir une personne ouvrir un article du média américain Techcrunch intitulé « Apple affirme qu’aucun utilisateur ayant activé le mode Isolement n’a été piraté à l’aide d’un logiciel espion ». Il s’agit bien entendu d’une petite provocation. La personne quitte ensuite cette page et accepte via AirDrop un document PDF qui n’est autre que le CV d’un chat. The applications cater to Tata Motors' internal combustion engine (ICE) and electric vehicle (EV) customers, respectively, and provide access to connected services such as remote vehicle commands, vehicle status, health monitoring and trip information.
CERT-In identified four vulnerabilities involving hardcoded credentials, inadequate URL validation, exposure of authentication tokens in application logs and improper implementation of SSL certificate pinning.
According to the advisory, these flaws could allow attackers to extract credentials and access backend services, obtain authentication tokens to impersonate users, or intercept and modify communications between the applications and their backend systems.

articles.summary:
La taxe de 5,5 centimes par gigaoctet disparaît du texte du budget transmis au Sénat. De quoi éloigner le risque d’un surcoût pour les plateformes, qu’elles auraient pu répercuter sur leurs clients.
Les gigaoctets de vos séries, jeux vidéo et autres téléchargements échappent, à ce stade, à la nouvelle taxe votée fin octobre. La proposition ne figure pas dans la version du budget qui va être examinée par les sénateurs. Elle tombe avec le rejet du volet recettes du projet de loi de finances pour 2027, intervenu mercredi 4 novembre à l’Assemblée nationale.
La taxe qui inquiétait les internautes sort du texte
Adoptée le 30 octobre, cette taxe sur les données transmises aux internautes français devait faire payer aux fournisseurs de contenus 0,055 euro pour chaque gigaoctet envoyé. Streaming vidéo, téléchargements de jeux ou réseaux sociaux auraient notamment été concernés.
Le dispositif ne prévoyait pas de prélèvement direct sur la facture Internet des particuliers. Ce sont les entreprises distribuant les contenus qui auraient dû s’acquitter de cette contribution. L’inquiétude concernait plutôt leur réaction : absorber le coût, modifier leurs offres ou augmenter leurs prix pour le reporter sur leurs clients.

If you have built anything that needs both a system of record and fast analytics, you know the shape of the problem. Postgres® holds the orders, the accounts, the state your application cannot afford to get wrong. ClickHouse software answers the questions.
A row store tuned for transactions was never built to answer at speed: what happened across a billion events in the last hour, which cohort is churning, what the agent should do next. Both engines are excellent at their jobs. The misery lives entirely in the gap between them.
“Both engines are excellent at their jobs. The misery lives entirely in the gap between them.”

articles.title: Why Testing Automated Driving Is Harder Than It Looks
articles.summary:
Instead of waiting for rare situations to occur on public roads, engineers can create those situations virtually.
Most people assume the hardest part of automated driving is building the technology itself. After all, enabling a vehicle to recognize traffic signs, detect pedestrians, stay within its lane, and react to complex traffic situations sounds like an extraordinary engineering challenge.
It is.
But many automotive engineers would argue that the bigger challenge comes afterward. How do you prove the system works safely?
As vehicles become increasingly software-defined, validation has become one of the most important and demanding aspects of ADAS development. ADAS validation is the process of evaluating whether driver assistance functions behave reliably across relevant driving scenarios, environmental conditions, system configurations, and software versions. The challenge is no longer simply creating intelligence. It is demonstrating that intelligence performs reliably across an almost limitless variety of situations.
Imagine a new ADAS function successfully navigating a busy urban environment. The vehicle detects traffic signs, maintains safe distances, and responds appropriately to nearby vehicles and pedestrians. Does that mean the system is ready?
Not necessarily. A single test drive represents only one combination of conditions:

articles.title: Sécurité : contournement de mot de passe sur Alpine Linux et musl — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Décidément, il semblerait que les briques les plus fondamentales de l’informatique moderne soient toutes pétries de failles de sécurité. À peine remis de la faille PHP qui a mis à terre un bon nombre de serveurs web, voilà que c’est le protocole SSH qui fait des siennes, remarque Ars Technica.
C’est plus spécifiquement une certaine implémentation de cet outil qui est concernée, notamment celle utilisée par Alpine Linux, une distribution largement déployée sur certains NAS, routeurs, objets connectés ou images Docker.
À vos mises à jour
Utilisé pour se connecter à une machine distante via la ligne de commande, le protocole SSH est extrêmement répandu dans le monde Linux. Son implémentation varie de système à système, mais, dans le cas qui nous intéresse, c’est l’interaction entre OpenSSH et musl, une bibliothèque C, qui est vulnérable. D’autres conditions doivent aussi être réunies (un mot de passe hashé via SHA256 ou SHA512 entre autres), mais ces dernières sont assez classiques sur les systèmes se reposant sur Alpine Linux.
Si ces conditions sont remplies, il suffit alors aux pirates de rentrer n’importe quel mot de passe de plus de 256 caractères et la connexion sera validée. De manière très simplifiée, cela se produit parce qu’un mot de passe de cette longueur provoque une erreur qui renvoie le caractère « * » au système, qui est incidemment le signe utilisé pour les comptes ne se reposant pas sur un mot de passe.

articles.title: GhostMap Android flaw lets malicious app trigger persistent boot loop
articles.summary:
Attackers can force Android devices into a continuous boot loop using a specially crafted app that requires no permissions and only needs to be installed.
To cause the persistent denial-of-service (DoS), the app triggers a vulnerability that researchers dubbed 'GhostMap' that makes Android map a file into an unallocated memory region. The affected process crashes when it attempts to read from that region.
Romanian cybersecurity company Bitdefender discovered the flaw while analyzing an Android banking trojan that kept crashing its emulators when it tried to read an application resource.
The researchers demonstrated the vulnerability by creating an app that contains no executable code, requests no permissions on installation, and does not need to be launched on the device.
According to the company, Google has been aware of GhostMap since August but closed the issue without releasing a patch, classifying it as "not reproducible."
Making phones unusable
In a report today, Bitdefender explains that GhostMap stems from two Android libraries that interpret ZIP compression methods differently. This allows a malformed APK (Android package file) to bypass size checks and be mapped beyond the file’s actual contents.
"Reading such an entry causes a SIGBUS (a signal sent by the CPU to stop a process that accesses an invalid memory space) in whichever process touches the file," the researchers say.

In an AI factory, high bandwidth memory (HBM)is the fastest, most expensive, and most contested memory tier. Every byte spent on a redundant weight copy, an idle session’s KV cache, or a recomputed prefix is a byte that is not being used to produce tokens. The question is no longer how much memory a GPU has, but how much useful work each byte delivers.
The generational data in Figure 1 below shows why. From GB300 to NVIDIA Rubin, capacity held at 288 GB while bandwidth rose to 19.2 TB/s.
agentic throughput per megawatt grew far faster. On SemiAnalysis AgentX, which replays recorded coding-agent sessions with real tool-call gaps and growing context, NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 then delivers up to 30x the throughput per megawatt of GB300 NVL72 at 160 tokens per second per user.
Capacity alone cannot explain a 30x gain delivered from the same 288 GB per GPU. The difference is how much useful work each byte delivers.
NVIDIA treats this as a co-design problem that spans GPU architecture, the scale-up interconnect, serving software, the CPU, and storage. This post examines five ways that co-design maximizes the value of each byte of memory, from the bits that encode a single weight to the shared storage that preserves and reuses context across agentic turns and nodes.

AI agents are moving from answering questions to taking action, and to do that effectively, they need to know the state of the business at any given moment. Most data architectures still aren’t designed to support querying subsecond updates across the enterprise, which is why the streamhouse has emerged to address this gap.
The streamhouse is a data architecture pattern that continuously delivers the current state of a business to applications and AI agents. A group of data infrastructure companies defined it to provide consistency around an approach many organizations have started to deploy independently anyway.
A streamhouse can be built from open-source technologies such as Apache Kafka, Apache Flink, and Apache Iceberg, from commercial products, or from a combination of both. The group behind it, which includes Confluent, Aiven, StreamNative and Ververica, has published an open, vendor-neutral definition at streamhouse.com, and anyone may use the name free of charge.
A common definition gives architects and data teams shorthand for what capabilities they need and where they sit relative to the rest of the stack. When a data engineer says “we need a streamhouse,” the CFO and other stakeholders can immediately understand what they mean and grasp the value.

Des chercheurs utilisent les impuretés du métal recyclé pour améliorer ses propriétés. Sur 17 variantes de fonte proposées par leur méthode d’apprentissage automatique, puis fabriquées et testées, 14 offrent un meilleur compromis entre résistance et capacité à se déformer avant de casser.
Pour obtenir un bon alliage recyclé, les industriels diluent souvent les impuretés de la ferraille avec du métal neuf. Une équipe réunissant plusieurs universités chinoises et l’Institut Max-Planck pour les matériaux durables a choisi de tirer parti de ces éléments indésirables. Ses travaux, publiés dans Science Advances, utilisent l’IA pour trouver les compositions et les traitements qui leur donneront un rôle utile.
Composer avec les impuretés plutôt que les diluer
Ajouter du métal primaire aide à retrouver les propriétés recherchées, mais sa production consomme de l’énergie et émet du CO2. Une partie de l’intérêt environnemental du recyclage se perd donc dans l’opération. articles.title: Closing the Identity Gap at the Service Desk
articles.summary:
Organizations have invested heavily in securing employee logins. Multi-factor authentication (MFA), conditional access policies and other identity controls make it harder for attackers to gain unauthorized access. But these protections can be undermined if the process for recovering access isn't held to the same standard.
When an employee needs to regain access to their account, it’s often the service desk that provides the password reset or account recovery. Yet identity verification commonly still relies on knowledge-based questions, such as an employee's manager's name or department.
This creates a gap in identity security where a weaker route into an account can bypass stronger login security. And as social engineering attacks become more convincing, that gap is becoming increasingly dangerous.
Why Knowledge-Based Verification Can No Longer Be Trusted
Attackers can gather a surprising amount of information before making a call. LinkedIn profiles, company websites, social media and leaked data can reveal everything from job titles and colleagues to office locations and personal details.
Armed with this information, an attacker can answer verification questions correctly and appear to be a legitimate employee.
This becomes particularly dangerous when passing these checks is enough to authorize a password reset or recover an account. An attacker could gain access to that account without ever needing to compromise the employee's original credentials.

The French Blood Establishment, or EFS, said “temperature and defrosting thresholds were raised to extremely high levels” on Monday at three of its cold-storage sites for plasma, in a statement released late Tuesday. Monitoring systems quickly detected the problem, allowing staff to take action in time so that “no blood products or samples were compromised,” it said.
French weekly newspaper Le Canard Enchaîné, which first reported the cyberattack, said that the attack had attempted to reset temperatures that normally are at minus 30 Celsius (minus 22 Fahrenheit) to as high as 110 C (230 F).

“No health consequences have been identified, and no blood products were lost,” the blood bank said.

articles.title: How CNC Machines Quietly Changed the Way Furniture Gets Made - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
Walk into a furniture workshop today and the first thing you notice is what’s missing. The noise. Not the absence of it, exactly, but the pattern. Instead of the stop-start rhythm of a circular saw and someone swearing at a mitre, there’s a steady mechanical hum that lasts twenty minutes and then stops.
That hum is a CNC router. And over the past fifteen years or so, it has rewritten how cabinets, tables, shelving and shopfitting get built, without most people outside the trade noticing.
From Pattern Templates to Code
CNC stands for computer numerical control, which is a dull name for something fairly clever. A designer draws a part on screen. Software converts that drawing into coordinates. A spindle spinning at 18,000 RPM then follows those coordinates across a sheet of material, cutting shapes to within a fraction of a millimetre.
Before this, repeat work meant templates. A cabinetmaker building forty identical kitchen doors would make a jig from plywood, clamp it down, run a router around the edge, unclamp, reposition, repeat. Accurate enough, but the jig wore down. Part number one and part number forty were never quite twins.
Digital files don’t wear out. That single fact changed the economics of small-batch furniture completely.
Why Tolerances Suddenly Mattered

The semiconductor industry is rapidly transitioning to chiplet-based architectures to meet the performance, bandwidth, and power demands of AI and high-performance computing (HPC). Technologies such as TSMC CoWoS, SoIC, Samsung I-Cube, X-Cube, Intel EMIB, and Foveros enable designers to integrate multiple compute, memory, and I/O dies into a single package, dramatically increasing system capability while reducing development risk.
As these architectures become more complex, signal integrity has emerged as a critical design challenge. High-speed die-to-die (D2D) interfaces, dense microbump arrays, silicon interposers, TSVs, and advanced package substrates introduce electromagnetic effects that can significantly impact performance, power efficiency, and product yield.
Traditional design methodologies that verify dies, packages, and interconnects independently are no longer sufficient. Success requires a system-level approach capable of validating complete communication channels spanning dies, interposers, package substrates, and memory stacks.

Following this week’s midterms where voters resoundingly voiced their opposition to data center expansion, OpenAI today announced new commitments to communities where it is working on data center projects, including that it won’t use non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with public officials.
OpenAI is stepping back from NDAs for data center projects
The ChatGPT maker won’t use NDAs with public officials as part of its new data center community commitments.
Many data center projects have come under scrutiny for relying on NDAs to hide discussions between developers and local officials. However, OpenAI says it is now allowing “only narrow protections covering legitimate security information, trade secrets, or proprietary or competitively sensitive information.” In October, Amazon announced it would no longer use NDAs with government agencies it works with on data center projects.
OpenAI’s additional commitments include paying “the full cost” of electricity it uses and the “infrastructure needed to serve us.” It will make opportunities for local communities by publishing the jobs it expects to create and by reporting on hiring. In Supermärkten in ganz Europa heizen Hacker Tiefkühltruhen auf bis zu 50 Grad hoch. Dafür brauchten sie keine KI, nur veraltete Steuerungstechnik, die offen im Netz hängt. articles.title: Bank Phishing Sites Show Fake ‘Suspended’ Pages to Evade Takedowns
