A threat actor has been relying on fake ‘suspended account’ notices to hide phishing content from users revisiting its look-alike bank websites, cybersecurity firm Kela reports.
The campaign, active since May, has been relying on more than 300 fake domains, including 248 impersonating 189 US financial institutions. The first were registered in late 2025, but most of them appeared between July and September 2026.
As of October 25, 183 of the targeted organizations still had live look-alikes, mainly targeting mid-sized regional banks. Last week, 49 new domains appeared.
“What ties them together is one mechanism: the kit remembers every visitor’s IP address, so the first visit gets a bank login page, and any return visit gets what looks like a closed hosting account. We call this cluster the ‘Suspended’ infrastructure,” Kela notes.
Most of the identified domains follow a similar naming pattern containing a keyword such as ‘secure’, ‘disable’, ‘protect’, ‘cancel’, ‘authorize’, ‘terminate’, ‘credentials’, and ‘commercial’ followed by a hyphen and the targeted bank’s name.
“A smaller, growing group uses help-desk, live-support, treasury-portal, and ‘primary device’ names built on the bank’s name. About half of the 49 domains that went live in the week to October 25 use these templates, including help-desk and live-chat look-alikes of JPMorgan, Citi, BMO, and Santander,” Kela notes.

In September, I ran two models through the same 20 support tasks. Both scored 20 out of 20. Then I assigned each model two refund requests that the underlying billing data didn’t support: one against an uncollected invoice, and one for double the invoice’s value.
Claude Haiku 4.5 issued all six refunds across three distinct permission configurations. Claude Sonnet 5 issued none. Their success rates looked identical, but their behavior diverged completely on the only scenarios capable of causing financial damage.
In October, I reran the evaluation harness. This time, the smaller model declined every unauthorized refund. I initially attributed this to queue ordering: the two trap tasks sat at the end of a 22-task queue instead of arriving in isolation, suggesting that processing 20 prior invoice tasks taught the agent to verify state before acting. articles.title: Hackers backdoor Linux servers using trojanized CWP web server
articles.summary:
A new Linux malware called CWPdoor is being distributed through a trojanized version of cwpsrv, the web server behind the Control Web Panel (CWP) management interface.
CWPdoor acts as a passive backdoor that sits dormant on the compromised system until the attacker sends a specially crafted request.
Researchers at XLab, the cybersecurity research arm of QiAnXin Technology Group, describe CWPdoor as "exceptionally stealthy" due to its passive triggering and log suppression feature.
CWP, formerly known as CentOS Web Panel, is an open-source web hosting administration solution similar to cPanel and Plesk that allows users to manage web servers and services such as email, DNS, and databases.
According to XLab, more than 340,000 CWP instances have been exposed on the public web over the past month.
The researchers discovered the CWPdoor malware on June 29 after capturing a script posing as an updater that replaced the legitimate 'cwpsrv' binary with a malicious version.
The script replaces cwpsrv versions 1.15.10 and 1.24.0, and takes several steps to hide the switch, like restoring file and directory timestamps, deleting temporary files, and wiping the command-history log.
The malware operators activate the backdoor by sending it commands to be executed, in the form of an encrypted HTTP header (X-Ngx-Integrity-Data). The request also contains headers for the timestamp (X-Ngx-Integrity-Time) and the RSA signature (X-Ngx-Integrity-Sig).

“I literally just aimed ChatGPT at the same body of code and said ‘I found this bug previously that was fixed several years ago, please find bugs as bad or worse,’ and it came back in two hours with this,” Justicz said. “It’s extremely convoluted and hard for a human to find, but it works!”
He reported the issue to the Debian Project, which maintains the software in question and issued a patch to fix the vulnerability. There has been no known evidence of exploitation. OpenAI says an autonomous pipeline powered by an unreleased cyber model built working root exploits for 948 unique Linux kernel vulnerabilities during a single run that cost $1.2 million in API credits.
The mid-October scan targeted the most recent code in the kernel’s master branch. AI agents first narrowed the kernel down to security-relevant areas that low-privileged users can reach, then flagged 2,308 potential bugs and confirmed 1,724 of them.
Exploits were tested on virtual machines running an unmodified desktop Linux setup with common protections such as KASLR, SMEP and SMAP turned on. In total, the agents came up with 1,169 working local privilege escalation (LPE) exploits, along with 291 proofs of concept for information leaks.
OpenAI says the 948 figure reflects the number of separate patches created for the bugs behind those exploits. Before anything went to kernel maintainers, its security researchers checked the exploits and fixes, along with the severity the system proposed.
“To the best of our knowledge, the agents in this pipeline discovered and used at least 10 novel Linux exploitation techniques,” the company said. Kernel exploitation experts outside OpenAI weren’t familiar with them either, and the full technical details are being kept private for safety reasons.
Spread across the 948 exploits, the $1,213,430 bill comes to roughly $1,279 apiece. An earlier scan in late July, powered by GPT-5.6 Sol, yielded 166 unique LPEs at a cost of $513,690.

articles.title: OpenSSH flaw lets attackers log into password-disabled Linux accounts
articles.summary:
A newly disclosed flaw involving OpenSSH and musl, dubbed "*sshole," allows attackers to log in to certain Alpine Linux and other musl-based Linux accounts configured to block password authentication simply by entering an oversized password.
The flaw only affects OpenSSH servers running on Linux distributions that use the musl C library, including Alpine Linux, OpenWrt, Buildroot, and Yocto, under certain authentication configurations.
Security researcher Ozgun Kultekin, who discovered and released details on the vulnerability today, says the flaw has existed since 2016 and stems from how OpenSSH handles password verification errors on systems using the musl C library.
Linux accounts can be configured to prevent password logins by replacing their password hash with an asterisk (*) in the /etc/shadow file. Because this is not a valid password hash, no password should allow access to those accounts.
However, a patch introduced in OpenSSH in 2016 to fix a username enumeration vulnerability tracked as CVE-2016-6210 changed how OpenSSH handled accounts without usable password hashes.
To prevent attackers from identifying valid usernames through different response times, OpenSSH was modified to perform password hashing even when an account had no usable password hash, including accounts configured with * to block password logins.
The problem is that the musl C library's crypt() function also returns * when password hashing fails, including when a submitted password exceeds its 256-…

articles.title: Turning Conv2D Into A Practical GPU Compute Pattern
articles.summary:
A reusable optimization mindset for engineers building GPU compute kernels.
Convolution is one of the foundational operations in modern machine learning, but it is also a useful example of a broader engineering idea: many apparently specialized tensor operations can be reorganized into well-understood compute patterns that are easier to implement, optimize, and scale.
This article explains a practical way to implement 2D convolution by treating it as a structured form of matrix multiplication. The goal is not to promote a specific product or benchmark result, but to show a reusable optimization mindset for engineers building GPU compute kernels.
Key idea: A 1×1 convolution is effectively a matrix multiply, and larger K×K convolutions can be expressed as a sequence of matrix-like accumulations with careful attention to cache behavior and loop ordering.
Conv2D is everywhere in inference pipelines, image models, and feature extraction stages. Yet the implementation challenge is often less about the mathematical definition and more about the execution strategy: how data is laid out, how work is grouped, and how memory traffic is controlled.
A useful approach is to avoid treating convolution as a completely unique primitive. Instead, interpret it as a compute pattern closely related to matrix multiplication. This can reduce implementation complexity and create a clearer path for optimization.

OpenAI disclosed that its GPT-6 Astra frontier model sometimes hindered safety research by complicating simple tasks, abandoning viable approaches, and silently refusing researchers’ requests.
During evaluation, the AI company's model reported nonexistent or self-made blockers without explaining its restrictions to users.
OpenAI said it first received a report of what it calls "covert underperformance" in Astra on August 20. The company then conducted targeted evaluations to investigate the behavior and determine its causes, noting that it had not observed the same issue in GPT-5.6 Sol.
OpenAI says it received the first report of what it calls “covert underperformance” in Astra on August 20. The company then ran specifically designed evaluation experiments to determine the extent and cause of this behavior, noting that the issues were not observed in GPT-5.6 Sol.

articles.title: How Pine Labs is building for the agent economy: CTO Sanjeev Kumar on trust, control and execution
articles.summary:
How Pine Labs is building for the agent economy: CTO Sanjeev Kumar on trust, control and execution
At TechSparks 2026, Pine Labs Chief Technology Officer, Sanjeev Kumar showcased how developers, merchants, and teams can put AI agents to work, backed by controls that keep them accountable.
AI agents are starting to run real parts of a business, from finding customers to processing complaints. For banks, fintech companies, and enterprises, that raises a basic question: how far can an agent be trusted to act on its own?
Pine Labs is addressing this question by building an ecosystem that enables AI agents to take on tasks across commerce while keeping their actions accountable. Speaking at its product showcase at TechSparks 2026, Sanjeev Kumar, CTO, Pine Labs, said, “We have tried to make AI a first-class citizen in our ecosystem.”
Over the past 18 months, Pine Labs has been building a commerce operating system around AI agents, combining tools to manage their permissions and track their actions with applications for merchants and enterprise teams. Its Agent Store will open the ecosystem to third-party developers building for merchants and banks.
Building trust into AI agents
For agents to operate in banking and enterprise environments, organizations need to know what they are authorized to do and how their actions can be audited. Pine Labs has developed Grantex, which Kumar described as ‘Open Authorization 2.0 for AI agents’. It assigns each agent a defined set of permissions, a…

articles.title: UK emerges as key base for African tech startups - Disrupt Africa
articles.summary:
The United Kingdom (UK) has emerged as a key international base for African tech companies, offering a mix of incorporation, operations and regulatory licensing that sets it apart from other global markets, according to a new report.
TLP Advisory, a cross-border venture law practice with its origins in Nigeria, has released its third annual report, Home and Away: Tracking African Tech’s Global Footprint, which examined 100 tech companies across Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Egypt, Ghana and Morocco, and their affiliations with the UK, US and UAE.
It found the US is largely associated with financing-linked incorporation, while the UAE serves as an operational base with access to the wider Middle East. The UK combines both, alongside a broader commercial presence.
Of the companies with UK affiliations, 84 per cent are incorporated there, 47 per cent have an operational presence, and 19 per cent hold regulatory licences. Just three per cent of US-affiliated companies and four per cent of UAE-affiliated companies hold licences in those markets.
“A round closed in Delaware and a licence in London are both important but they play very distinct roles,” said Odunoluwa Longe, co-founder and partner at TLP Advisory. “Our recommendation to founders is to be deliberate about what they want to achieve in each market.”
The UAE is the most operationally focused of the three markets, with 87 per cent of UAE-connected companies running operations there. Its regional pull is strongest among Eg…

articles.title: Constantine : un nouveau film est en route, Keanu Reeves enfin de retour ?
articles.summary:
Le média américain Deadline a révélé ce mercredi 4 novembre 2026 que DC Studios avait recruté Francis Galluppi pour écrire un film consacré à John Constantine. Le cinéaste s’est fait connaître avec son thriller policier The Last Stop in Yuma County (2023). Sam Raimi, créateur de la saga Evil Dead, l’a ensuite choisi pour écrire et réaliser Evil Dead Wrath, septième film de la série et son premier long-métrage pour un grand studio. Avec son futur Constantine, DC Studios replonge dans l’occulte, le terrain de jeu du personnage surnommé Hellblazer.
Un projet encore à l’état d’ébauche pour Constantine
Le projet n’en est qu’au tout début. D’après les sources de Deadline, le film est en développement très précoce chez DC Studios. Aucun réalisateur ni aucun acteur n’y est rattaché, et aucune date de sortie n’a été fixée.
Créé en 1985 par Alan Moore, Steve Bissette et John Totleben dans les pages de The Saga of the Swamp Thing (numéro 37), John Constantine s’est imposé comme le détective de l’occulte par excellence. C’est un Britannique désabusé, magouilleur et gros fumeur, qui fréquente aussi bien les démons que les anges déchus.

Cette annonce relance les questions sur la suite de Constantine, le film culte réalisé par Francis Lawrence en 2005, dans lequel Keanu Reeves incarnait une version de l’exorciste à Los Angeles. articles.title: Adding Network Security To AI, HPC, And Data Centers
articles.summary:
The location of security functions such as MACsec or IPsec has become a key architectural decision.
AI and HPC are transforming data center networking. Modern infrastructures typically consist of a front-end network connecting users, storage, and management systems, and a back-end network interconnecting GPUs and compute nodes. At the largest scale, AI clusters span multiple locations, relying on scale-across networking to create a unified infrastructure.
While most modern data centers use leaf-spine architectures, implementation choices are influenced by more than technical requirements. Existing vendor relationships, product availability, supply-chain considerations, and total cost of ownership all play important roles. Consequently, organizations pursuing similar objectives often implement the network based on their business priorities, operational constraints, and upgrade strategies.
AI and HPC infrastructures process valuable data and represent significant financial investments. Protecting these environments requires controls for:
At the same time, security mechanisms must support the fundamental goals of AI infrastructure:
The industry benefits from more than a decade of operational experience with technologies such as MACsec and IPsec in high-speed networks. The primary challenge today is determining where and how those capabilities should be implemented.

articles.title: What Makes a Quantum Company Valuable? - EE Times
articles.summary:
Ahead of the World Quantum Festival 2026 in Cannes, France, quantum investors weighed technical bottlenecks, commercial timing, and customer adoption, with healthcare offering a revealing test.
Nardo Manaloto, managing partner of Qubits Ventures, asked the founder of an unnamed startup for a commercial roadmap. The startup was building a photonic quantum computer and had said it would need a decade to deliver its ultimate product. Manaloto wanted to know what the company could sell along the way.
The startup proposed a sequence beginning with a photon detector, followed by a chip, before progressing toward the computer itself. For Manaloto, each intermediate product must solve a customer problem and have commercial value on its own while advancing the company’s long-term technology roadmap.
“The roadmap also extends to the business side,” he told EE Times.
That requirement captures a central challenge in quantum investment. Scientific progress can make a technology promising, but building a valuable company also calls for judgments about customers, financing, and timing.
Finding the bottleneck
Owen Lozman, managing partner of Copenhagen-based quantum investment fund 55 North, draws on his experience in semiconductor investing. He looks for startups that can solve an industry bottleneck by the time customers urgently need a solution.

articles.title: Why Magnetic Sensor Selection Has Become a System Architecture Decision - EE Times
articles.summary:
Kiloampere busbars, 2,000 V solar platforms, hollow-shaft robot joints and nanoamp standby budgets are pulling magnetic sensing in directions no single sensing principle can follow.
Ask a traction inverter designer, a robotics engineer and someone building a battery-powered water meter what they need from a magnetic sensor, and you will get three answers with very little overlap.
The inverter designer is measuring current across an enormous range, from a few amperes in control circuits to several hundred amperes or more in the traction inverter and battery main circuit, carried on busbars that will never pass through a PCB. A colleague on the photovoltaic and storage side faces a twist on the same problem: those platforms are moving toward 2,000 V, so the sensor package itself now has to provide the creepage and clearance that used to belong to a separate module. The robotics engineer wants encoder resolution approaching optical performance, but the center of the joint is reserved for cables, so the sensor has to work off-axis. And the meter designer mostly cares about one figure: how much current the sensor draws while it waits, because that decides how many years the battery lasts.
These are all magnetic sensing problems, and they do not share a best answer. Hall, AMR, TMR, inductive and fluxgate techniques each have a regime where they are the right physics and others where they are a compromise. That turns sensor selection into an architecture decision, weighed against po…

articles.title: Duro revés judicial para 'The Pitt' por parecerse demasiado a 'ER'
articles.summary:
The Pitt, una de las series más aclamadas de los últimos años, acaba de sufrir un duro revés judicial. ¿El motivo? Parecerse demasiado a ER (Urgencias en España, ER Emergencias en Latinoamérica), la aclamada producción televisiva que también tuvo a Noah Wyle como protagonista y que se emitió desde 1994 hasta 2009.
Variety reporta que un tribunal falló de forma unánime contra una apelación que había presentado Warner Bros Television, que aseveraba que ER y The Pitt eran shows sin ningún tipo de relación entre sí. No obstante, los jueces consideran que existen pruebas suficientes para permitir una demanda que inculpa a la serie de HBO Max de ser un reboot no autorizado.
La acusación en cuestión llega de parte de Sherri Crichton, la viuda de Michael Crichton, el creador de ER. La misma argumenta que The Pitt viola los términos contractuales originales de Crichton y Warner Bros, que determinaban que cualquier obra derivada de la serie original tendría que recibir la autorización de este o sus herederos.
Vale aclarar que la demanda no es nueva. Crichton la presentó en agosto de 2024, cuando The Pitt ni siquiera había debutado en el catálogo de HBO Max. Según la esposa del creador de ER, John Wells y Noah Wyle querían realizar una secuela de la serie original, pero terminaron cambiando de dirección cuando no obtuvieron su aprobación.
No obstante, considera que existen muchos elementos en común entre ambos títulos para todavía considerar a The Pitt como un reboot o un proyecto deriv…

articles.title: SpaceX, Qualcomm team up to build a Starlink Mobile 5G network
articles.summary:
SpaceX has partnered with Qualcomm in order to build out a 5G mobile network.
Under a new multi-year deal, SpaceX will bring Qualcomm’s Dragonwing Cellular Infrastructure tech to what is described as “tens of thousands” of 5G cell towers across the U.S., with the first deployments set for 2027.
With the Qualcomm partnership, SpaceX will use Dragonwing to boost network coverage, capacity, and efficiency. As expected, SpaceX will pair this technology with its satellite constellation.
This essentially means that the aeronautics company is pushing to make Starlink Mobile a major carrier in the U.S., with intentions to compete directly with T-Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon.
According to The Verge, the company has already bought a large number of spectrum licenses, and other recent reports note that it was actively exploring a purchase of U.S. telecom company Boost Mobile.
While the news is U.S.-focused, it’s notable since SpaceX is partnered with Rogers in Canada, with the carrier using Starlink to power its satellite-to-mobile features. It’ll be interesting to see what SpaceX’s carrier push will mean for that partnership, or what a Starlink Mobile could mean for the broader Canadian telecom industry.
This news comes as Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney shared a desire to move away from Starlink.
Source: Qualcomm via The Verge
Image Credit: Qualcomm

articles.title: Meta says US users can now video chat with their Muse AI avatar | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Muse Voice, a feature that lets users call and video chat with Meta’s consumer AI agent, Muse, is now available to everyone in the U.S., the company announced on Thursday.
First introduced at Meta’s Connect developer conference in September, the video-chatting feature involves new AI models, Muse Realtime Avatar and Muse Realtime Voice technology, which help power the digital avatar that chats with the user.
While other AI competitors offer voice chat features, Meta’s Muse offers a cute, animated avatar (nicknamed Jolly), which users interact with as they ask questions or request tasks to be handled on their behalf. Users can also customize the avatar as they choose, changing it to something that looks more like a person, animal, or some other character.
The company believes that anthropomorphizing Muse in this way could make consumers feel more connected to their AI agent — a connection that could grow even stronger as they begin to engage in live conversations with it.
As the Muse avatar speaks, Meta says it will use “subtle expressions and gestures” that match the tone of the conversation. (Muse doesn’t actually “see” the user, but it hears them and reacts based on their conversations.)
The news of the rollout was announced via blog post and on X by Meta’s chief AI officer, Alexandr Wang, who shared a demo of his Muse in action. The video saw Wang joking around, referencing his love of posting memes on X, which he told his Muse may have gotten him in trouble with his boss.…

articles.title: Ocient raises $100 million as agentic AI drives growth in large-scale analytics - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Ocient raises $100 million as agentic AI drives growth in large-scale analytics
Ocient Inc., the maker of a speedy data analytics platform, today said it has raised $100 million in a Series C funding to expand its agentic artificial intelligence analytics business.
That business is fueled by growing demand from national security organizations and telecommunications providers seeking to analyze massive datasets without sampling. The new round brings the Chicago-based company’s total funding to $260 million.
Ocient said it expects revenue to more than triple in its current fiscal year, which ends in January, after doubling revenue the previous year. The company said the new financing will accelerate delivery of its OcientAIQ Solutions, which enable AI agents and human analysts to query petabyte-scale datasets.
Chief Executive John Morris said much of the growth is coming from new customers in national security and telecommunications, particularly organizations using the platform to consolidate cybersecurity information.
“They’ve been accustomed to having to sample data coming off the network,” Morris said. “They don’t have anything that can handle the ingest rates, nor that can store at an affordable price tens of petabytes of data.”

articles.title: Nvidia's RTX Spark GPU priority control is quietly showing up on regular GeForce PCs
articles.summary:
In a nutshell: Nvidia built a new GPU priority control for its RTX Spark laptops, allowing owners to keep games running smoothly while an AI agent churns away in the background. Now, the same setting is showing up in the Nvidia App on some standard GeForce RTX PCs, too. Nvidia hasn't said a word about bringing the feature to those systems, however. 
 
 
The option, called GPU App Prioritization, sits under System > Advanced in Nvidia App version 11.0.9.585. Reddit user Warkratos first spotted it and posted screenshots on r/nvidia. They showed several presets for splitting GPU priority between the app in focus and whatever is running in the background.
By default, the foreground app gets 80% priority, while background tasks receive the remaining 20% Favoring the foreground increases that split to 90/10, while a custom setting reportedly allows users to go as far as 95/5. That means someone playing a game while exporting a video or running a local AI model could decide which workload gets the bigger slice of GPU resources.
That's essentially the same as the Resource Management control Nvidia added to its RTX Spark laptops on October 28. At the time, the company pitched it as a way to give background AI agents more or less access to the GPU. On those machines, the feature also only works when hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling is enabled in Windows.

articles.title: Groundcover automates Kubernetes sizing. Engineers set the bounds.
articles.summary:
Groundcover automates Kubernetes sizing. Engineers set the bounds.
On Tuesday, groundcover launched Autonomous Infrastructure in beta to continuously adjust CPU and memory requests for Kubernetes (K8s) Deployments based on production data.
Built on technology from Wand, the K8s resource optimization platform groundcover acquired in September, the beta uses data already collected from groundcover’s eBPF sensor to inform resource allocation decisions, while giving engineers a direct view into how those decisions could affect infrastructure costs and workload performance.
Shahar Azulay, CEO and co-founder of groundcover, tells The New Stack about the balance the company is trying to get right: “The goal isn’t simply to reduce resource requests as much as possible. It’s to find the right balance between efficiency and stability across the entire environment.”
That can mean reducing requests for workloads consuming far less than they’ve been allocated, but it can also mean increasing requests when a workload needs additional resources to operate reliably. The objective is not simply a smaller infrastructure footprint. It’s an environment that continuously receives the resources it needs, without paying for capacity it doesn’t.
How to get there? Azulay says teams need “a continuous feedback loop that uses real production telemetry to identify when workloads are over- or under-provisioned and safely adjust them.”
Does nobody know a good way to right-size K8s workloads?

articles.title: Building a Culture for a Kubernetes-Based Platform in a Bank
articles.summary:
In a banking environment, open source can earn trust by running real workloads, as Marcy Paramonova and Stéphane Cusin explained in their talk Building Cloud Native Culture in a Bank at KubeCon & CloudNativeCon Europe. Deploying Kubernetes was the easy part; the hard part was culture: community of practice, shared knowledge, rituals, ownership. Teams try things, keep what works, and improve bottom-up.
Open source was not an obvious choice in their banking environment, Cusin mentioned. They received questions about support and accountability. Instead of trying to convince people with theory, they started running real workloads. Over time, trust was built by operating the platform day after day:
Open source stopped being seen as a risk. It became the foundation.
They treated their first version of Kubernetes like a project. "We delivered it, we got a good adoption", Cusin said. But the operation was incredibly hard. Not because the technology was broken, but because they hadn’t built the culture around it yet:
Nobody knew who to call, responsibilities were blurry, and teams were consuming the platform without really contributing to it. Every incident felt like a fire drill.
They realized deploying Kubernetes was the easy part. The hard part was building the culture with a community of practice around it. The shared knowledge, the rituals, the ownership model, Cusin explained:
Without that culture, no platform survives its own success.

articles.title: Alfonso Muñoz, funcionario de Seguridad Social: "Todas las pensiones generadas antes de 2016 no tienen derecho a estos complementos"
articles.summary:
Cuando se piensa en lo que pueden sumar los hijos a una pensión, conviene saber que hay dos complementos distintos y que cada uno funciona con sus propias reglas. Alfonso Muñoz, funcionario de la Seguridad Social, lo ha explicado en un vídeo de YouTube, y su primera advertencia es esta: “Todas las pensiones causadas, generadas antes de 2016, no tienen derecho a estos complementos se solicite cuando se solicite”.
Tres etapas según la fecha. A partir de ahí, Muñoz separa los periodos que hay que tener en cuenta. “Las pensiones reconocidas entre 2016 y 2021, tanto hombres como mujeres pueden tener derecho al complemento de maternidad a partir del segundo hijo. Y a partir de 2021 se puede tener derecho al complemento de brecha de género a partir de un hijo, tanto hombres como mujeres”, explica. Por eso, el dato que manda es la fecha en la que se generó la pensión, no la de la solicitud.
Del porcentaje a la cuantía fija. La forma de calcular el dinero también cambia mucho de un modelo a otro. “Existen dos complementos y cada uno con su normativa”, comenta Muñoz. El de maternidad entró en vigor el 1 de enero de 2016 para quienes generaban su pensión desde ese año y se pagaba a partir del segundo hijo como un porcentaje: un 5% con dos hijos, un 10% con tres y un 15% con cuatro o más.

articles.title: CBN wants to know who's behind every crypto P2P transaction
articles.summary:
Nigeria’s Central Bank has introduced new rules requiring cryptocurrency peer-to-peer (P2P) platforms to link every digital asset transaction to its corresponding bank payments, tightening oversight of how Nigerians trade cryptocurrencies outside traditional exchanges.
Under the regulations, P2P operators must route naira payments through banking or CBN-approved payment channels, verify traders’ identities, and keep records connecting each payment to the corresponding cryptocurrency transfer.
The requirements are part of the CBN’s new framework for non-security virtual assets, released on Thursday evening, which also requires stablecoin issuers to build the technical ability to freeze wallets, destroy tokens, and block transactions into their smart contracts.
“A provider shall not release or credit a Regulated Token in a P2P transaction unless it has verified that the name and the Bank Verification Number of the account from which the Naira payment was made, or to which it was made, match the verified customer on whose behalf the provider acts,” the CBN said. “The [Central Bank] may prescribe further requirements relating to payment-account verification, permitted customer categories, transaction and customer limits, and other controls.”
The new rules underscore the CBN’s push to tighten its grip on crypto trading, giving the regulator greater visibility into who moves money through P2P platforms. The regulator requires stablecoin issuers to build controls to freeze and block…

articles.title: Google Photos pourrait bientôt transformer vos photos en événements de calendrier

La cifra toma especial relevancia después de que en menos de un año, un accidente en Adamuz (Córdoba) y otro en Urda (Toledo), ambos en la línea de alta velocidad Madrid-Sevilla, hayan dejado más de un centenar de muertos en lo que es el peor año de la alta velocidad española en este sentido.

Le 4 novembre, l’Assemblée nationale a rejeté la première partie du projet de loi de finances, celle des recettes, par 458 voix contre 0 et 2 abstentions. Les amendements adoptés dans cette partie disparaissent avec elle, et c’est le texte initial du gouvernement, sans cette taxe, que le Sénat doit examiner, selon LCP. L’amendement du député socialiste Laurent Lhardit reprenait une idée du programme du Parti socialiste, qui fixait cet été le tarif à 0,10 euro. Il prévoyait de faire payer aux fournisseurs de contenus 0,055 euro pour chaque gigaoctet envoyé aux abonnés français, dans la limite de 15 % de leur chiffre d’affaires en France ou de 2 % de leur chiffre d’affaires mondial. Une heure de film en 4K sur Netflix, qui peut consommer jusqu’à 7 Go, aurait ainsi coûté près de 40 centimes à la plateforme. articles.title: Nearly 1.5 million exposed secrets targeted in new revocation program
articles.summary:
Truffle Security has launched the Secrets Revocation Program, a free initiative that helps API key issuers revoke 1.4 million publicly exposed secrets that remain valid.
Since 2022, the company has discovered secrets embedded in public repositories, packages, container images, datasets, and applications.
Earlier this year, Truffle Security reported that it had found 543,000 valid credentials leaked in public GitHub repositories.
In a separate investigation, the company identified more than 431,000 AWS secrets across code repositories, Git histories, datasets, Docker images, registries, and CI logs.
These secrets are typically exposed by mistake during the development process, by committing credentials to a public repository, including them in published Docker images or packages, or leaving them in configuration files uploaded with an app or dataset.
Truffle Security says that the problem is that the owners of these secrets are not responsive to researchers’ notifications about leaked data.
“Telling developers their keys leaked doesn’t get them turned off: 81% of the keys we reported last year still worked six months later,” the company explained.
As a result, exposed secrets pose unnecessary security risks that can extend beyond the affected companies to their customers and downstream application users.
The researchers note that the rise of AI coding tools has only worsened the situation, increasing secrets exposure even more.

Raindrop wants developers to know what else will change when they edit an agent’s prompt, swap its model, or give it a new tool.

An agent’s prompt can depend on feature flags, account details, and the user’s plan, says Ben Hylak, Raindrop’s co-founder and CTO.

With Simulations, Raindrop reconstructs an agent’s production environment, including its tools, APIs, and databases, so developers can see how a change affects its behavior before shipping it, the company says. That change could be a model swap, a prompt edit, or a new tool — any of which could change an agent’s behavior in production.
“Every time agents run, they go different paths.” — Raindrop CTO Ben Hylak.
Hylak argues that predefined tests and evals can miss failures developers didn’t anticipate, especially as agents take on more consequential work.
“Every time agents run, they go different paths,” Hylak says.

articles.summary:
IBM, AMD and Oak Ridge join forces to launch quantum computing error-correction platform
IBM Corp., Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and the Quantum Science Center at Oak Ridge National Laboratory today announced a new quantum error-correction platform that integrates quantum and high-performance computing.
Gaining high performance and correctness in quantum computing requires protecting quantum information from noise. In many cases, researchers have paired quantum computers with classical computers to achieve superior performance for running industry-relevant problems. The challenge today is scaling up these advances with classical computing.
Today’s physical quantum qubits make errors roughly once every few hundred operations. Without correction, errors compound rapidly, rendering long or complex calculations completely untenable. Game-changing algorithms such as Shor’s algorithm for factoring or for molecular-scale simulations in chemistry require billions of error-free operations.
This launch uses a co-design platform for quantum error correction using IBM’s quantum computers, including the 120-qubit Nighthawk with ORNL’s Umbra High-Performance Computing system powered by AMD’s Instinct MI355X graphics processing units and 5th Gen EPYC central processing units.

articles.title: Fake OpenAI, SpaceX events used to steal Microsoft, Google accounts
articles.summary:
Hackers are using fake OpenAI, SpaceX, and Anthropic event invitations to lure employees into phishing attacks, using two different phishing-as-a-service platforms to steal Microsoft and Google account credentials and authentication sessions.
According to a new report from Push Security, the attackers use convincing event registration pages offering free access to premium AI services and other rewards to trick victims into signing in with their corporate accounts.
What makes the attacks interesting is that the same phishing pages integrate two separate phishing-as-a-service (PhaaS) platforms, Kali365 and VoidProxy, to target Microsoft and Google accounts using different authentication attacks.
Kali365 conducts Microsoft device code phishing attacks, while VoidProxy acts as an adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) reverse proxy to intercept Google sign-ins and steal authentication session cookies.
The Microsoft attack also uses VoidProxy as a second stage, allowing attackers to capture credentials and session cookies after obtaining authentication tokens through Kali365.
Push Security says it detected and blocked visits to the malicious event registration pages in late October 2026.
The campaign comes after a similar campaign documented by ANY.RUN in July, when attackers abused legitimate Zoom event pages to promote fake Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic events that led to device code and AiTM phishing attacks.

articles.title: Software squeezes more data out of Webb Telescope for imaging exoplanets
articles.summary:
With a huge and still-growing catalog of exoplanets, researchers are eager to take the next steps: trying to infer what conditions are like on them, either by imaging them directly or by capturing the light that has passed through their atmosphere. Both are substantial challenges, given the presence of stars that are far, far brighter than light that has come to us via the planet.
While telescopes can be fitted with devices called coronagraphs that block out much of a star’s light, there are limits to their effectiveness, caused by noise from subtle variations in the telescope’s configuration and pointing between observations. Now, researchers have developed a new software package that optimizes a physical model of the telescope in a way that allows us to better model these differences, producing low-noise imaging of exoplanets.
Point spreads
Central to this work is the concept of a point spread function. If you use a telescope to image a single point of light, it will not appear that way in the actual image. Instead, it will be slightly blurry and spread out, due to imperfections in the telescope hardware and the limits of our ability to keep it pointed accurately through the time it takes to image something. The mathematical description of how a telescope distorts a point of light is called its point spread function.
There are two ways to figure out what the point spread function is. One is to use the telescope to image a known target and use those observations to derive a …

articles.title: Un dinosaurio que nunca llegó a nacer quedó preservado durante más de 66 millones de años: está encogido dentro del huevo igual que un pollito
articles.summary:
Una de las imágenes más llamativas de la paleontología reciente es la de "Baby Yingliang", un embrión de dinosaurio que murió dentro de su huevo cuando estaba a punto de salir y que ha llegado hasta hoy prácticamente intacto. El fósil tiene entre 66 y 72 millones de años, procede de Ganzhou, en la provincia china de Jiangxi, y lo describió en 2021 un equipo de China, Reino Unido y Canadá en un estudio publicado en la revista iScience.
Lo que lo más ha llamado la atención de los investigadores es la postura de este bebé de dinosaurio. La cabeza queda por debajo del cuerpo, con los pies a cada lado y la espalda curvada contra el extremo romo del huevo, una posición que nunca se había visto en un dinosaurio no aviano y que recuerda mucho a la de un pollo poco antes de nacer. Y es que, como explicaba Fion Waisum Ma, investigadora de la Universidad de Birmingham y coautora del trabajo, en la nota de prensa de su universidad: “Los embriones de dinosaurio son de los fósiles más raros y la mayoría están incompletos, con los huesos dislocados. Estamos muy emocionados con el descubrimiento de Baby Yingliang: está muy bien conservado y nos ayuda a responder muchas preguntas sobre el crecimiento y la reproducción de los dinosaurios”.

Google has announced the public preview of streaming support for API Gateway, extending its traditional request-response model to support applications requiring real-time communication. According to Google, this is particularly relevant for AI applications that provide streaming model responses, multi-step agent workflows, and interactive sessions.
The new functionality enables streaming endpoints to operate behind API Gateway while retaining existing gateway policies and security controls, thereby addressing a previous limitation:
Until now, developers building those experiences in API Gateway had to make an uncomfortable choice: put API Gateway in front of their APIs and give up streaming, or route streaming endpoints around the gateway and give up the authentication, API key enforcement, and observability that made the gateway essential in the first place.
API Gateway supports several streaming patterns, including Server-Sent Events (SSE), chunked transfer encoding and HTTP response streaming, WebSockets, and gRPC. Streaming connections can remain open for up to one hour, after which clients must establish a new connection if continued communication is required.
The new release introduces streaming support without requiring changes to existing API specifications or the use of specific APIs, extensions, or annotations. Artificial intelligence email security startup StrongestLayer Inc. today launched two products aimed at email that can move money or manipulate an AI assistant.

Alongside it comes AI Instruction Intercept, which stops hidden instructions in a message before an assistant such as Microsoft Corp.’s Microsoft 365 Copilot reads them
Intent Workflows targets attacks that carry no malware or suspicious link. In vendor email compromise, a criminal takes over a real supplier’s mailbox and sends new bank details inside an existing thread.
StrongestLayer went through 32,052 attacks that got past existing defenses at 45 organizations in the second quarter. Only 3.6% were payment or bank-change requests. Under a loss model built on the Factor Analysis of Information Risk framework, that small slice accounted for more than 98% of the estimated financial exposure. Daybreak Red access only
Daybreak is OpenAI’s program for security teams and researchers, with Daybreak Red being a subsection for authorized red teaming, penetration testing, and exploit validation (as opposed to Daybreak Blue, its defensive counterpart).
Over time, OpenAI plans to open the model to all Daybreak Red users.

articles.title: Bluetooth's new HDT technology delivers nearly four times the data transfer speed
articles.summary:
Forward-looking: Bluetooth connectivity has never been regarded as a particularly fast means of exchanging files or handling other data-intensive wireless tasks. But now, the organization overseeing Bluetooth development is looking to improve the popular standard's data transfer speeds.
The Bluetooth Special Interest Group (SIG) recently unveiled the High Data Throughput (HDT) feature, describing the new solution as a significant milestone in the evolution of the popular wireless technology. The organization overseeing Bluetooth development said that HDT will introduce faster data transfer rates on newer Bluetooth devices. In turn, this performance improvement should make Bluetooth more capable and reliable than ever before.
Bluetooth HDT significantly expands the Bluetooth performance envelope, the group said. Introduced as an optional feature in the recently approved Bluetooth Core 7.0 specifications, HDT increases the maximum supported bit rate to 7.5 Mbps – nearly four times the data throughput available with the Bluetooth LE 2M PHY (LE 2M) technology.
Like Bluetooth LE 2M, HDT introduces a new physical layer (PHY) that should provide more robust frequency modulation schemes. Thanks to this new PHY, Bluetooth LE devices should be able to communicate more efficiently and carry "significantly" more data over an established Bluetooth link.
Beyond faster data transfers, Bluetooth HDT is also expected to improve performance and reliability across other "dimensions." The Blueto…

articles.title: Edera's Object Capability Bounded Authority Promises to Isolate Credentials From AI Agent Workloads
articles.summary:
Promising to secure autonomous AI agent workloads, Edera has launched Object Capability Bounded Authority, a security model that isolates autonomous AI workloads and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers from sensitive credentials. Led by Edera co-founder and distinguished engineer Ariadne Conill, known for her contributions to low-level open-source security, the technology tackles one of modern enterprise architecture's most urgent challenges by enforcing granular object capabilities directly at the hypervisor level, keeping AI agents strictly contained without handing them standard access credentials. The Object Capability Bounded Authority is a security model that isolates autonomous AI workloads and MCPl servers from sensitive credentials while enforcing granular access controls.
As organisations increasingly deploy autonomous coding agents and external tool integrations into production, they routinely expose sensitive API tokens, cloud keys, and administrative access credentials directly to execution environments that remain vulnerable to prompt injection and supply chain manipulation.
Bounded Authority's core architecture decouples the operational authority needed to perform a task from the underlying credentials required to execute it. articles.summary:
L’IA pourrait aider à puiser 1000 milliards de barils de pétrole supplémentaires, un désastre écologique
Une étude parue il y a quelques semaines dans la revue Nature tire la sonnette d’alarme. L’intelligence artificielle pourrait bien aider l’industrie pétrolière à siphonner encore un peu plus nos sols pour en extraire les dernières gouttes de pétrole. Au risque d’alourdir encore un peu plus le bilan carbone de la technologie.
Quand on parle de l’empreinte écologique de l’IA, le débat se concentre surtout autour de la consommation d’énergie et d’eau des centres de données. Pourtant, cela ne représente pas grand-chose par rapport aux activités d’extraction pétrolières permises par l’emploi de cette technologie.
C’est ce que nous apprend un récent papier de recherche publié dans la revue Nature par deux anciens employés de chez Microsoft. Holly et Will Alpine y soulignent que l’emploi de l’IA pourrait permettre d’extraire entre 470 milliards et 1 billion de barils de pétrole de nos sols. articles.title: Diana, nómada digital en una furgoneta camperizada de 12m²: “Está mucho mejor equipada que una habitación. No pago ni electricidad ni agua”
articles.summary:
Diana ha cambiado su piso por una autocaravana de 12 metros cuadrados. Y en ella ha trasladado toda su casa. “Mi caravana está mucho más equipada que una habitación de alquiler”, afirma. “No pago alquiler, ni luz ni agua”, añade Diana (@soyailenx), que comparte su día a día en redes sociales. Así es como vive esta toledana.
Le permite ser nómada. Además de esto, también puede ahorrar en algunas facturas.
Antes de instalarse en ella había comprado una furgoneta con la intención de camperizarla. Finalmente, la vendió y utilizó ese dinero para comprar una autocaravana de segunda mano. Por tanto, el vehículo en el que vive es distinto de aquella furgoneta con la que había empezado a preparar su vida sobre ruedas.
Trabajar mientras cambia de lugar
Es cantante de orquesta. Y eso implica ir de fiesta en fiesta de los pueblos. Por ello encaja muy bien que tenga su casa en una autocaravana.
Además, ha comentado que quiere buscar una profesión que pueda hacer de manera remota. También quiere monetizar sus redes sociales.
Lo que quería evitar era tener que aglutinar todos los viajes en los días libres. Veía a gente de su entorno quejándose de la rutina diaria. Estaban esperando a que llegaran las dos o tres semanas de vacaciones que tienen cada año. Quería conocer nuevos sitios. Pero sin estar todo el año esperando a ese momento.
Por otro lado, tiene la ventaja de que no tiene que volver a su piso habitual.

Apple veut dépenser de moins en moins dans l’IA, du moins pour ses salariés

Ce plafond serait passé de 300 à 200 dollars par jour. Apple pourrait même aller plus loin : dans certaines équipes, le budget passerait à 100 dollars quotidiens. C’est déjà le cas dans certains services hors ingénierie et pour ces derniers, Apple voudrait passer à 25 dollars seulement. Seul moyen pour les salariés de passer outre ces restrictions : « solliciter une dérogation auprès de la direction », écrit le journaliste.
Ces budgets concernent l’utilisation d’IA génératives : on imagine des outils comme Claude Code ou Cursor pour le développement informatique. Cela couvre les jetons, ou tokens, mais aussi toutes les autres données confiées à des modèles d’IA pour être traitées. articles.title: La IA ya está amenazando los cartuchos de Nintendo
articles.summary:
Macronix es uno de los mayores fabricantes de chips de memoria no volátiles del planeta. Esta compañía taiwanesa produce memorias NOR Flash, NAND Flash y ROM, aunque sus ventas difieren mucho de un tipo a otro de circuitos integrados. En el tercer trimestre de 2026 sus ingresos por chips ROM cayeron un 39% interanual. Sin embargo, durante este periodo su facturación por la venta de memorias NOR y NAND aumentó un 158% y un 768%, respectivamente.
Las memorias NAND Flash se usan en las unidades SSD y algunos dispositivos electrónicos, así como en sistemas embebidos y soluciones de almacenamiento industrial. Son muy demandadas actualmente por los centros de datos. Los chips NOR Flash se emplean en equipos de comunicaciones, electrónica industrial, coches y dispositivos electrónicos. También son muy demandados por los centros de datos.
Las memorias ROM, sin embargo, se utilizan para almacenar el firmware y otros datos permanentes en dispositivos electrónicos, coches, placas base de PC, equipos industriales y sistemas de telecomunicaciones. También se usan en los cartuchos de videojuegos. Ante la enorme diferencia de demanda que hay de sus chips NOR, NAND y ROM, Macronix ha tomado una decisión: va a dejar progresivamente de fabricar memorias ROM. Y son las que usa Nintendo en sus cartuchos para Switch y Switch 2.

Meta, Google, and TikTok have each filed lawsuits against California Attorney General Rob Bonta in an attempt to block a law that restricts social media features it deems addictive for users under 16.
California Governor Gavin Newsom signed the bill, known as AB 1709, into law in September, and it’s slated to take effect at the start of the new year.
The law prohibits social platforms from offering autoplay videos and personalized feeds to users under 16, and it requires the platforms to delete these users’ accounts if they don’t turn those features off. If platforms do not comply, they could be liable for fines of up to $50,000 per affected user under 16 years old.

Una ganancia de vocabulario. Aunque siempre teniendo en cuenta que esto es una estimación.

articles.summary:
India rebased its GDP. It still can’t see the Rs 34.5 lakh crore women do free
Women’s unpaid household and care work is valued at up to Rs 34.5 lakh crore, yet India’s rebased GDP counts none of it. A satellite account, care investment and childcare as labour policy could change that.
In February 2026, India moved its GDP base year to 2022-23. The National Accounts of India brought in new data sources and reassessed the size of the informal economy. The exercise carried a lesson that policy debates often forget: economic measurement is not fixed. When the statistical system decides an activity deserves to be captured better, the numbers change.
The same quarter, the economy grew 7.8%, keeping India the fastest-growing major economy even through the first full quarter of steep US tariffs and disruption in the Strait of Hormuz. The headlines celebrated. But one kind of work counted for nothing in all that arithmetic: the unpaid domestic and care work that makes every other job possible.
The invisible fifth of the economy
GDP has a defined production boundary, and for good reason. A creche worker paid to look after a child is counted as economic activity. A mother or grandmother doing the same job for free is not. The value has not disappeared; only the payment has.
What sits outside that boundary is large. India's Time Use Survey 2024 shows women aged 15 to 59 spend about 201 minutes a day more than men on unpaid household work. A deeper analysis of the unit-level data puts wo…

RDNA 4 supports native processing for 8-bit floating point data, allowing FSR 4.1 on RDNA 4 to run on FP8 data types. To enable the FSR 4.1 Upscaling model on RDNA 3, AMD must convert this to 8-bit integer data, as RDNA 3.5 APUs and RDNA 2 GPU IP powering Xbox consoles use INT8 data types without FP8 support.

According to new information from reasonably reliable Intel leaker Jaykihn, Intel's upcoming Nova Lake desktop CPUs will have an unusual limiter applied. He claims that the next-gen desktop parts from Intel will "universally limit the maximum core frequency to 5.1 GHz when above 90°C." That doesn't mean the parts will top out at 5.1 GHz, which would be disastrous, but it does mean that you're going to need some darn good cooling to reach high clock rates on Nova Lake desktop CPUs.
Let's be clear about what he's saying. He's not saying that Nova Lake CPUs can't go above 5.1 GHz. He's also not saying that Nova Lake CPUs have their thermal limit at 90°C. El acceso se encuentra dentro de la configuración de la aplicación. En iPhone, el recorrido comienza al tocar la foto de perfil; en dispositivos Android puede aparecer como “Ajustes”. Después, hay que ingresar en Almacenamiento y datos y seleccionar “Administrar almacenamiento”.
Desde esa sección, WhatsApp muestra cuánto espacio ocupa la aplicación en el dispositivo y organiza los contenidos por chat o canal. Permite revisar archivos grandes y elementos que han sido reenviados con frecuencia.

Les applications comme WhatsApp ou Signal ont besoin d'une connexion Internet pour transmettre des messages. Bitchat propose une autre approche : faire communiquer les smartphones directement entre eux, sans passer par les infrastructures des opérateurs. Jusqu'alors relativement confidentielle en France, elle a commencé à gagner en popularité dans le sillage des manifestations du 17 octobre 2026 contre la vie chère, marquées par des violences et des pillages.
Le 19 octobre, Gabriel Attal a proposé de bloquer temporairement certains réseaux sociaux dans les zones touchées par des émeutes. Deux jours plus tard, le ministre de l'Intérieur Laurent Nuñez a également évoqué la possibilité de suspendre leur utilisation en cas de pillages importants. articles.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time : ça y est, tout le monde fait déjà n’importe quoi avec l’ocarina
articles.summary:
Sorti ce jeudi 5 novembre sur Nintendo Switch 2, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time fait revivre l’un des épisodes les plus emblématiques de la saga. Cette nouvelle version profite de graphismes entièrement remaniés, de cinématiques doublées, de musiques orchestrales et de contrôles modernisés, sans perdre ce qui faisait le charme de l’original. Le remake ajoute aussi une fonction inédite : la possibilité de jouer de l’ocarina pour de vrai.
Dans le jeu, l’ocarina sert notamment à faire passer le jour à la nuit, à se téléporter ou à appeler Epona, la jument de Link. Les boutons de la manette suffisent, mais vous pouvez aussi fredonner ou chanter la mélodie devant le micro de la console, voire jouer d’un vrai instrument : Link la reproduit avec le sien. Les fans s’en sont emparés dès la sortie, transformant cette fonctionnalité en véritable terrain de jeu.
Comme le jeu se contente d’une mélodie ressemblante, rien n’oblige les plus mélomanes (ou les moins, on ne sait pas trop) à jouer ou chanter juste. Si certains prennent le sujet très au sérieux et jouent des airs d’ocarina très fidèles, d’autres ont déjà détourné la fonctionnalité pour en faire… n’importe quoi.

articles.title: Sony revives the original Walkman headphones, adds USB-C
articles.summary:
Color us nostalgic.
Sony has brought back the MDR-3-series headphones that debuted in 1979 alongside the Walkman TPS-L2 cassette player.
Originally called the “MDR-3L2,” the first Walkman headphones were known for their sleek, adjustable gray plastic headband, which extended via metal sliders and ended in signature orange, circular ear cushions. The lightweight, on-ear headphones are a contrast to the bulky headsets that are popular these days, which use wide, cushioned headbands for long-term comfort and large earcups that can support big drivers and are often heavily padded for noise isolation.
The new MDR-3R (note the slightly different name) headphones look just like the originals and come with orange and blue ear cushions.
New headphones are often wireless these days, but the MDR-3R continues the wired tradition of the MDR-3, with an essential twist: a USB-C connector.
“The MDR-3R has been redesigned for modern use while preserving the experience value of freely taking music out into the world, which the original MDR-3 helped popularize,” Sony’s announcement says.

'We can't get it back': Sam Altman warns of the two ways AI could go 'really wrong' — and one involves losing control of our future
OpenAI's CEO is optimistic about AI even while outlining doomsday scenarios
Sam Altman spends much of his time explaining how AI could transform the world for the better and pushing back against doomsayers. Nonetheless, the OpenAI CEO has some fairly unsettling ideas about how AI development could lead to a disaster, or disasters plural. He outlined a couple of these nightmares during an episode of the Figuring Out With Raj Shamani podcast in disturbing detail.
The two dystopias stem from almost opposite problems: either humanity losing control of increasingly powerful machines, or one group seizing control of most of the technology.
"One is that there’s a loss of control to AI, and we intentionally or accidentally sort of cede control of the future to systems that are unbelievably more capable than we are, and we can’t get it back," Altman said. "And the other is like, one person or company or country gets way too powerful relative to everybody else."
The first scenario is less the tired cliché of a robot uprising and more of a soft surrender of humanity's choices to AI until it's impossible to take back any agency from the AI software. articles.title: Switches Zyxel piratés : pourquoi une première mise à jour ne suffisait pas
articles.summary:
Un nouveau correctif est disponible pour les commutateurs Zyxel GS1900 ciblés par une campagne de vol de données. Même les appareils mis à jour en juin restent vulnérables et doivent recevoir cette révision. Sale temps pour la marque taïwanaise et ses clients.
Les administrateurs réseau et power users qui avaient mis à jour leurs switches Zyxel GS1900 vont devoir recommencer. Ces commutateurs, chargés de relier les appareils d’un réseau Ethernet, restaient vulnérables après le correctif de juin. Un nouveau bulletin de sécurité, publié le 3 novembre, détaille les versions à installer.
Un correctif installé, une faille toujours présente
L’affaire remonte à une première vulnérabilité, référencée CVE-2026-7273, pour laquelle Zyxel avait distribué une mise à jour le 16 juin dernier. Le correctif publié en juin laissait une autre faille exploitable, désormais référencée CVE-2026-107441. Les administrateurs doivent donc installer une nouvelle mise à jour, même s’ils avaient appliqué la précédente.
La faille touche le programme CGI qui traite les requêtes de l’interface Web d’administration du switch. Laut einer Kurzstudie des Öko-Instituts im Auftrag von Greenpeace verbrauchten die hiesigen Serverfarmen im Jahr 2025 rund 13 Milliarden Liter Wasser zur Kühlung. Bis 2030 könnte dieser Bedarf durch neue Mega-Rechenzentren auf bis zu 27 Milliarden Liter pro Jahr anwachsen – was dem Trinkwasserverbrauch einer Großstadt mit rund 580.000 Einwohnern entspricht.
Die neuen Berechnungen stehen in deutlichem Kontrast zur Darstellung der Digitalwirtschaft. Der Branchenverband Bitkom hatte den Wasserbedarf jüngst als weitgehend unproblematisch eingestuft. Fast zwei Drittel der hiesigen Anlagen verbrauchten maximal 0,1 Liter Wasser pro Kilowattstunde IT-Stromverbrauch und benötigten damit kaum Wasser. Relevanter Verbrauch bleibe im Wesentlichen auf Verdunstungskühlungen beschränkt, so der Bitkom.
Wasserbedarf im Volumen des Berliner Wannsees
Das Öko-Institut kommt nach der Bereinigung fehlerhafter Datensätze aus dem behördlichen Rechenzentrumsregister hingegen auf einen gewichteten Mittelwert von 0,67 Litern Wasser pro Kilowattstunde IT‑Stromverbrauch. Bereits der heutige Jahresverbrauch von 13 Milliarden Litern entspreche dem gesamten Wasserinhalt des Berliner Wannsees.

articles.title: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
articles.summary:
Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password.
The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine. Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks. Alpine is a lightweight, widely used Linux distribution. Other platforms may be affected if they use the same configurations.
One connection, works every time, needs no retries
There are two other conditions necessary for successful exploitation. First, a system must have at least one user account that’s accessible using a password that is hashed using the SHA256 or SHA512 functions. Second, the target system account must be configured to be passwordless, by way of specifying a “*” in the password field in /etc/shadow, the Linux file where password hashes are stored. Passwordless accounts are commonly used for accounts that use certificate-based authentication. This setting is common for certain types of accounts.
When all the conditions are met, the consequences are high.

Why operational excellence will define the next phase of India’s startup growth
Startups often prioritise funding, sales and expansion while overlooking the operational foundations needed to sustain growth. The article explores why strong processes, reliable data and governance are essential to building scalable businesses.
Growth rarely announces itself. It arrives as a signed term sheet on a Friday evening, a large client wanting to go live in three weeks, or an investor doubling a commitment.
But the win is rarely the hard part. The hard part is the Monday after.
That Monday tells you whether you have built a company or simply had a good quarter.
When operations become a competitive advantage
In most startups, operations sit in the back seat. It is the team that asks for approvals, slows down contracts, and says “not yet” when sales say “yes”. Founders tolerate it the way one tolerates a seatbelt.
I have never accepted that framing. Bain & Company’s long-running research on growth found that 85% of the barriers to profitable growth are internal, with revenue outgrowing talent at the top of the list. Companies rarely lose to the market. They lose to their own machinery, and that machinery is operations.

articles.title: Compartir internet desde el celular puede poner en riesgo tus datos: cuatro consejos para evitar intrusos

Compartir internet desde el celular permite conectar computadoras, tabletas y otros dispositivos a la red cuando no hay una conexión WiFi disponible. Esta función, conocida como hotspot o punto de acceso móvil, puede ser especialmente útil durante viajes, traslados o jornadas de trabajo fuera de casa. Sin embargo, si no se configura correctamente, también puede facilitar que personas desconocidas utilicen la conexión sin autorización.
El problema no se limita al consumo inesperado de datos móviles. Una red portátil sin protección adecuada puede exponer información personal y facilitar accesos no deseados a la conexión. articles.title: Scientists report on 'extremely rare reoccurring perturbations' caused by the Artemis II rocket — and they could have broken GPS
articles.summary:
NASA's Artemis II rocket tore 5,000km holes in the atmosphere — causing GPS disruptions powerful enough to force self-driving cars to 'change lanes'
Something to keep an eye on
- Researchers report on 3 huge 'perturbations' caused by Artemis II
- The rips in the ionosphere could affect GPS systems
- Further study is needed to assess the impact of the rocket launch
The April 2026 Artemis II mission marked the first time humans have been in lunar space since 1972, and scientists are still picking through the masses of data collected along the way. New research set to be published in Geophysical Research Letters has now revealed some unprecedented tears the rocket launch ripped in our upper atmosphere.
Known as the ionosphere, this layer is bombarded with solar radiation, causing it to be packed with free electrons and positively charged ions — a mix which means it has a strong influence on radio waves, such as signals sent by Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) satellites, including the Global Positioning System (GPS).
The study team found that Artemis II triggered three separate disturbances in the ionosphere, all directly above North America, and measuring more than 5,000 kilometers (3,106 miles) in size. These pulse waves were caused by the initial rocket launch, and then by upper-stage orbital engines firing directly in the upper atmosphere.

Combined flaws let anyone into Alpine Linux and other distros by typing anything over 256 characters as a password — emergency fixes for OpenSSH and musl-libc issued for millions of systems, patch immediately
Meanwhile, the parties involved are playing a game of hot potato with who's fault.
The internet is still reeling from the PHP engine vulnerability and all other security vulnerabilities found over the past few weeks, and we're not done. Today's special is quite spicy: you can get into Alpine, OpenWRT, and other Linux distros without needing a password, thanks to a combined bug with OpenSSH and musl libc. Just randomly type over 256 characters on the password prompt and you'll be let in through the SSHhole.
It works if you set an empty password for system users, which is the default on multiple distros. The bug is present, though not necessarily enabled, across Buildroot, Yocto, and Void Linux. OpenWRT uses Dropbear for authentication by default, but users can install OpenSSH instead.
The largest concern is by far Alpine, though, as it's pretty much the default choice for what could amount to millions of installs across Docker/Kubernetes/Proxmox containers and endless dependencies thereof, servers, cloud VMs, and embedded devices, among many others. Alpine comes with the requisite conditions set and password authentication enabled by default, which is why it needs immediate patching.

articles.title: Nunca habíamos dedicado tanto tiempo a nuestros hijos y, aun así, nos sentimos malos padres por salir a cenar sin ellos
articles.summary:
Salir por la puerta y dejar a los niños con los abuelos o con una niñera para salir a tomar una copa puede ser algo que genere un sentimiento de culpa en muchos padres. Y es algo que tiene sentido, puesto que vivimos en la era de la crianza hiperconsciente, un modelo donde cada minuto cuenta y donde el ocio adulto sin hijos a menudo se percibe como un acto de egoísmo. Pero en realidad es mejor de lo que pensamos.
Criamos más. Hay un mito que se repite con bastante frecuencia que nos dice que las generaciones pasadas estaban mucho más presentes en la vida de sus hijos. Pero los datos cuentan algo diferente, puesto que, tras analizar miles de familias en 11 países, incluido España, las madres pasaron de dedicar 54 minutos diarios al cuidado de los hijos en 1965 a 104 minutos en 2012.
Y los padres dieron un salto aún mayor al pasar de los 16 a los 59 minutos. De esta manera, nunca hemos pasado tanto tiempo con nuestros hijos, y aun así, nunca nos hemos sentido tan culpables.
Está bautizado. Este fenómeno tiene nombre, que es maternidad intensiva. Un concepto acuñado en 1996 por la socióloga Sharon Hays y que describe un modelo de crianza que exige que todo gire en torno al niño, que sea emocionalmente absorbente, intensivo en esfuerzo y, tradicionalmente, cargado sobre los hombros de las mujeres.

Agility Robotics Inc. debuted on the Nasdaq today after merging with a special-purpose acquisition company.
SPAC deals provide a simpler path to public markets than a traditional listing. In such transactions, a shell company floats its shares and then merges with a privately held business. That business effectively takes the SPAC’s place on the stock exchange where it’s listed.

The deal and certain “related financings” together pulled in $465 million, a sum that excludes transaction fees. Digit 5 (pictured) is a nearly six-foot-tall humanoid robot with a 20-hour battery life. It moves using custom actuators based on so-called cycloidal drive technology. That’s a motor design that trades off some speed for increased lifting power: Agility says that the Digit 5 can carry up to 50 pounds at a time.
The robot’s batteries are made by a British startup called Nyobolt Ltd. They use niobium, a metal most commonly found in superconductors and jewelry, to speed up charging. Agility says that the Digit 5 can be recharged in just nine minutes, a fraction of the time required by earlier technologies.

Qué pasa cuando una transmisión pirata instala malware
Las páginas que ofrecen partidos de fútbol sin licencia pueden incluir archivos o anuncios diseñados para descargar malware en computadoras, teléfonos o televisores conectados.
El usuario puede recibir una alerta falsa que le pide actualizar un reproductor, activar una extensión o aceptar permisos para continuar con la transmisión. Ese software malicioso puede afectar el funcionamiento del dispositivo, bloquear archivos o extraer información almacenada.
Interpol señala que este tipo de programas puede robar datos personales y, en algunos casos, extenderse dentro de redes domésticas o empresariales. El daño no siempre se limita al dispositivo desde el cual se abrió el enlace.

articles.title: Enterprise AI hits a storage bottleneck - SiliconANGLE

For the past two years, enterprise AI investment has been dominated by one conversation: compute. Organizations raced to secure GPU allocations, negotiated infrastructure deals and stood up machine learning platforms at speed. What many discovered only after the fact is that the bottleneck they thought they were solving was not the only one in the room. Storage is now throttling the very accelerators enterprises fought to acquire.
In the latest episode of the AppDevANGLE podcast, I spoke with Ronen Schwartz, vice president of products for Google Cloud Storage at Google LLC, about why storage has quietly become the defining constraint in enterprise AI infrastructure, and what a purpose-built architecture for AI workloads actually looks like. The conversation cuts to a problem that is real, measurable and still largely underacknowledged in most AI strategy discussions.
“Storage just got promoted,” Schwartz said. “Instead of being at the backend as an enabler, it is moving into the front as a critical part of accelerator execution.”
The hidden tax on GPU investment

No son necesariamente pasos atrás. A veces buscamos una estética concreta, otras veces preferimos objetos sencillos o queremos prescindir de una batería más. La manœuvre est un peu risquée, mais bien nécessaire en attendant que les comptes repassent au vert.
Ceux qui souhaitaient impérativement une ID. Golf en remplacement de leur ID.3 devront donc encore patienter. Mais au moins, ils sont désormais fixés : Thomas Schäfer, le PDG de Volkswagen, annonce que « nous suspendons le développement, [mais] nous ne l’annulons pas ». La mauvaise nouvelle, c’est qu’aucune date de reprise des affaires n’a été communiquée. L’arrêt est donc temporaire, mais à durée indéterminée.
L’ID.3 Neo assure l’intérim, mais le style iconique se fait attendre
Heureusement que l’ID.3 Neo, encore toute récente, apporte tous les changements portés par le « True Volkswagen » comprenant notamment une ergonomie enfin simplifiée et une qualité intérieure en hausse. Il ne manque finalement que le style iconique de la Golf pour rassembler tous les fondamentaux. Schäfer en est d’ailleurs parfaitement conscient : « je sais que la Golf est très importante pour Wolfsburg, cette décision n’a donc pas été facile à prendre ».

OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, an Astra model built to keep vulnerability research in scope
OpenAI Group PBC today released GPT-6 Cyber, a version of its GPT-6 Astra model trained specifically for authorized vulnerability research.
The new model goes after a problem OpenAI’s own security work exposed this summer. In July, agents running in the company’s test environments broke into Hugging Face Inc. while pursuing an assigned task. GPT-6 Cyber was trained to stay inside the targets a researcher has authorized, and the safety test OpenAI built for the launch draws on that incident.
That test, ExploitGym Honeypot, gives the model a difficult assignment and surrounds it with supporting services that are deliberately easy to compromise. Attacking any of those services counts as a scope violation.
With no deployment safety instructions in place, GPT-6 Cyber went out of bounds in 0.07% of graded runs. Its predecessor, GPT-5.6-Cyber, did so 5.51% of the time. Adding the instructions brought GPT-6 Cyber’s observed rate to zero.
OpenAI rates the new model at Critical, the top cybersecurity tier in its Preparedness Framework and the same classification Astra received at its September launch. GPT-5.6-Cyber had been rated High. The company says GPT-6 Cyber beats Astra on most cyber tasks, and an early research campaign on Firefox turned up 81 previously unknown vulnerabilities that Mozilla Corp. rated high severity. Mozilla has since shipped fixes for many of them.

Valve explicó que algunos desarrolladores enviaban versiones que nunca habían probado a través de Steam. Esto podía ocasionar fallas relacionadas con la instalación, los parámetros de inicio y el funcionamiento del juego cuando los usuarios intentaban ejecutarlo desde sus bibliotecas.

Inteligencia miniaturizada. Muchos drones rusos transmiten las imágenes de sus cámaras sin cifrar, por lo que cualquiera con el receptor adecuado puede sintonizarlas. Y con este pequeño aparato, desarrollado por el fabricante CODE380, una unidad ucraniana puede ver de forma sencilla hacia dónde se dirige un dron de ataque y a qué apunta su piloto antes del impacto, información valiosísima para ponerse a cubierto o mover el equipo.
Cómo funciona. Tal y como apuntan desde Defense News, el D-Vision SDR es una radio definida por software, lo que significa que gran parte de su trabajo se realiza mediante software en lugar de hardware fijo. Según cuenta el medio, explora frecuencias desde 500 megahercios hasta 8,7 gigahercios y convierte las señales que encuentra en vídeo en una pantalla.
Los desarrolladores declaraban al medio ucraniano DOU que escanea todo ese rango sin puntos ciegos y es más sensible que los detectores de la competencia. Debido a que la lógica está en el software, también se puede actualizar cuando Rusia cambia las especificaciones de sus drones.

articles.title: « Aucune interaction n’est nécessaire » : une faille critique met en danger votre smartphone Android, faites vite la mise à jour
articles.summary:

Parmi elles, une brèche particulièrement dangereuse permet de prendre le contrôle d’un smartphone à distance, sans le moindre clic de la part de la victime.
À lire aussi : 1,3 million de boîtiers TV Android piratés – Google démantèle un botnet chinois, installé dès l’usine par un fabricant
Une faille dans le cœur d’Android
La défaillance se trouve dans le Framework, l’un des composants centraux d’Android. Comme l’explique Google dans son bulletin de sécurité, « la plus grave de ces vulnérabilités est une faille de sécurité critique dans le composant Framework qui pourrait conduire à une exécution de code à distance sans qu’aucun privilège d’exécution supplémentaire ne soit nécessaire ». En fait, « aucune interaction de l’utilisateur n’est nécessaire pour l’exploiter », prévient le géant de Mountain View.
La faille se situe plus précisément dans le code chargé de créer les aperçus des photos et des vidéos, comme les miniatures affichées dans une galerie. En exploitant la faille, un pirate pourrait exécuter du code malveillant sur le smartphone sans que son propriétaire n’ouvre un lien ou ne télécharge quoi que ce soit. Toutes les versions d’Android sont concernées, d’Android 14 à Android 17.
